entries.title: fix(release): fail fast on publish prerequisites and harden the relea…
entries.content:
```
fix(release): fail fast on publish prerequisites and harden the release flow (#137637)

* fix(release): harden candidate tooling and Android pin checks

Prepare trusted release:candidate dependencies before loading the helper, reusing the target install only when lockfile bytes and dependency declarations match. Resolve tsx from the tooling checkout, clean up the shared link, and remove the late Parallels install.

Record stable Android train alignment from the frozen target in console, JSON, and Markdown evidence. Warn with the mobile preparation command when the pin lags while preserving independent Android publication.

* fix(release): recognize closeout PRs and tolerate full label sets

Recognize same-repository stable main closeouts by branch, title, published origin tag, and changelog section boundaries. Preserve published closeout text while retaining the explicit release automation override.

Treat exhausted GitHub label capacity as a visible warning for automatic PR size labeling, including concurrent HTTP 422 cap failures. Preserve unrelated API errors. These repairs cover the release closeout failures observed on PR #137506.

Validation: 87 focused tests, targeted types and lint, shell checks, standalone workflow guards, real closeout Git-object replay, and independent review. Full changed checking is blocked by an unchanged duplicate Vite type tree; workflow checking cannot install pinned pre-commit 4.6.2.

* fix(release): fail early on invalid publish prerequisites

Require the parent of core npm, plugin npm, and ClawHub publication to run
from its protected release-publish tooling tag. Remove the main-to-matching-
tag lookup and its obsolete tests. Docker-only recovery keeps main;
Tideclaw alpha and its separately approved main bootstrap keep their routes.
The candidate checklist also refuses regular publish commands without a
protected tooling tag and explains --publish-workflow-ref.

The old split gave parent approval refs/heads/main while children produced
tag provenance. scripts/openclaw-npm-postpublish-verify.ts:320-343 requires
exact approved ref/SHA agreement. The parent identity inputs are declared
at .github/workflows/plugin-clawhub-release.yml:41-48 and consumed at
.github/workflows/plugin-clawhub-release.yml:447-448.

Read apps/android/version.json from the release tag before qualification.
A stable train mismatch records one skip reason in the parent summary,
publish sequence, and release proof, and skips both native qualification
and Android publication. Matching pins retain genuine qualification failure
handling. Correction tags compare their base version. The summary directs
operators to scripts/mobile-release-version.ts --prepare before the next tag.

Before real ClawHub dispatch, query each active status separately so a stale
waiting child cannot be hidden by newer completed runs. Refuse with its URL
and the pending_deployments rejection/wait remedy. A read-only live call
caught waiting run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33812823818.
No workflow dispatch, deployment rejection, release, or push was performed.

Keep successful-parent detached children: the parent explicitly delegates
approval to the operator, and ClawHub's validateParentState permits
an automated-detached submission after parent success. Follow-ups: cleanup
of gates abandoned by failed/cancelled parents, and source-SHA correlation
across different tooling refs. The current conservative guard matches the
workflow ref because the run-list API does not expose dispatch inputs;
it does not claim to cover identical-source collisions across tooling tags.

Production/tooling +80/-49 (net +31), tests +245/-85 (net +160), docs +72/-32
(net +40). Remaining production growth owns the Android pin/skip fact and
ClawHub dispatch admission; the obsolete main fallback is deleted.

Validation (no dependency installation and no CHANGELOG.md edits):
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts
  Before fix: 2 new failures, 106 passed.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts -t 'keeps publish children|prevents a ClawHub dispatch'
  Before fix: 6 new failures, 3 passed.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts -t 'rejects main before|retains the matching Tideclaw|admits Android only'
  Before fix: 9 failures, 1 passed; mismatched pins incorrectly admitted native CI.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts
  Final: 500 passed. An earlier run passed 499 and caught one obsolete
  package.json-only sparse checkout assertion, removed from that table;
  the Android regression now owns its metadata checkout contract.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts -t 'keeps release history checks blobless|admits Android only'
  Passed 7 after correcting the obsolete checkout guard.
- bash -n scripts/lib/release-publish-children.sh: passed.
- shellcheck scripts/lib/release-publish-children.sh: 8 existing shared-global
  warnings/info; baseline had 9. No new findings.
- shellcheck --rcfile=config/shellcheckrc --severity=error scripts/lib/release-publish-children.sh: passed.
- pnpm check:workflows: blocked acquiring pinned pre-commit==4.6.2 from the
  configured Python index; actionlint/zizmor not available locally.
- node scripts/generate-ci-git-owner.mts --check: passed.
- python3 scripts/check-composite-action-input-interpolation.py: passed.
- node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs: passed.
- node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- .github/workflows/openclaw-release-publish.yml scripts/lib/release-publish-children.sh scripts/release-candidate-checklist.mts test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts docs/ci.md docs/reference/RELEASING.md
  Guards, formatting, script erasability and script types passed. Root test
  types remain blocked solely at unchanged ui/vitest.config.ts:188 by two
  incompatible Vitest dependency trees in the supplied symlinked install.
- pnpm check:coercion-helpers && pnpm lint:scripts: passed.
- node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts: passed after brace-only test lint cleanup.
- node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check .github/workflows/openclaw-release-publish.yml scripts/release-candidate-checklist.mts test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts docs/ci.md docs/reference/RELEASING.md: passed.
- git diff --check: passed.

Live publication was not exercised: it would publish release artifacts.

Independent Codex P1 autoreview of the final diff: scoped-clean, no
accepted/actionable findings. Review did not execute project code.

* fix(release): space the negated docker-only guard group

bash parses an adjacent "!(" inside [[ ]] as an extglob pattern when
extglob is enabled; the spaced form is the negation-of-group the guard
intends. Both branches proven with a direct bash evaluation.

* docs(release): require the protected publish tag and name the Android pin step

The maintainer skill now states that the publish parent must be dispatched
from the release-publish/<sha12>-<epoch> tag whenever children publish, and
that the Android train must be pinned before a stable tag or the release
cannot ship Android.

* test(release): drive the Android pin checks through the protected publish ref

The sandboxed coordinator fixtures now pass --publish-workflow-ref and stub
the tooling identity check, matching the publish-ref requirement the parent
and candidate helper now enforce.

* fix(release): seal a single ClawHub package from the flat artifact download

actions/download-artifact writes a lone pattern match directly into path
instead of path/<artifact>, so a one-package selected publish failed at
"Seal actual packed inventories" with ENOENT on the per-artifact directory
(child run 33816953287 for @openclaw/arcee-provider@2026.9.1). Resolve the
flat layout only for a one-entry matrix; multi-package matrices keep the
per-artifact directory contract.

* test(ci): route the labeler workflow to its size-label test

* fix(release): install trusted tooling dependencies in isolation

Linking the target checkout's node_modules into the trusted tooling worktree
let pnpm workspace package links resolve back into the target, so candidate
code could run inside the trusted helper. The tooling worktree now always
installs its own frozen graph (--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
--prefer-offline); the reuse branch and its lockfile comparison are gone.

* style(release): brace the packed artifact directory guard

* fix(release): validate the Android pin before it reaches workflow outputs

apps/android/version.json comes from the release checkout and its version
string was echoed into GITHUB_OUTPUT after only a non-empty check, so a
crafted value containing newlines could append output records (sha,
android_pin_matches) that downstream publication jobs trust. The step now
accepts only an exact YYYY.M.PATCH string and fails before writing any
output otherwise; the contract test drives injection payloads through the
real step script.

* fix(release): block requested ClawHub runs before dispatching another child

GitHub reports requested and action_required as active workflow-run states
before queued/waiting; the dispatch guard only checked waiting, pending,
queued, and in_progress, leaving a window for two real ClawHub publishers on
the same protected ref.
```

Pre-warm chrome-devtools-mcp@1.8.0 before browser-extension E2E and cache npm metadata plus the installed npx tree under the pinned package version. Configure the disposable checkout to use that absolute cache offline during the test, since npm otherwise revalidates metadata inside the 30-second MCP handshake. Add a contract derived from the runtime package pin and select it for workflow or runtime-pin changes. The final-head browser E2E, gateway regression, other CI jobs, focused contracts, and independent review passed. Peter explicitly waived the npm bulk-advisory timeout for this landing; the dependency audit did not pass. No CI policy or security checks were weakened.

Related incident: #137506. Runtime diagnostics and the browser-maintenance cold-load graph remain documented follow-ups in #137711.

Co-authored-by: Patrick Erichsen <patrick.a.erichsen@gmail.com>
```

entries.title: Good old days at OpenAI in 2016: an agent stares at screen pixels, moves a mouse, and books a flight...
entries.content:
Good old days at OpenAI in 2016: an agent stares at screen pixels, moves a mouse, and books a flight on United. We called it World of Bits, inside OpenAI Universe. 10 yrs later, Astra is reincarnated in the same universe. Even the naming is astronomically correct 😆  
  
Universe was perhaps the most ambitious AI infra project at the time, but we couldn't quite figure out how to solve it. A policy with zero prior knowledge of what a "submit" button does has to rediscover the entire internet visual lingua by trial and error. In retrospect, RL from scratch against hand-drawn, per-task "artisan" reward functions on a bunch of Pascal Titan X GPUs was completely doomed.  
  
To solve computer use agent, the right way turns out to be boiling the ocean first (hillclimb on every general task you can find), and then specialize back down to the screen pixels and keystrokes. Or simply, a "Specialized Generalist".   
   
Lessons learned: one step ahead of everyone, you're a pioneer. Three steps ahead, you're a prophet. Five steps ahead, you're a martyr.  
  
Congrats, GPT-6! That United flight finally gets booked, reliably this time. The 2016 intern in me has a big smile.

来自 ByteDance Seed 等团队的研究者们，发布了一个把评测对象从 "任务答案" 转向 "Agent 执行基础设施" 的基准「H...
entries.content:
LLM 能自己创建和演化 Agent Harness 吗？  
  
来自 ByteDance Seed 等团队的研究者们，发布了一个把评测对象从 "任务答案" 转向 "Agent 执行基础设施" 的基准「HarnessDev」  
论文：[huggingface.co/papers/2609.01…](https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.01437)  
  
现有问题  
同一模型换个 harness（执行循环、工具、上下文管理、恢复、验证），成绩可差十几个点，但现有基准都把 harness 当作固定配置，从未评测 "模型能否自己造 harness"。论文填补这一空白。  
  
基准设计  
· Creation：从一个只有被动工具、无任何策略、零分的弱种子出发，凭任务说明和 1–3 个样例构建完整 harness。  
· Evolution：从自建 harness 出发，用 189 个反馈任务的结果迭代 10 轮，自选最终版；之后在 630 个从未展示的任务上测泛化。  
· 创建者与执行者分离：Self-Eval（跑自己写的）vs Unified-Eval（统一用 Gemini 跑），前者测协同设计，后者测 harness 是否是可迁移资产。  
· 同时报能力与执行 token 成本；评分只看真实 diff/环境状态，harness 自报成功不计分。  
· 6 个创建者，4 领域 5 基准，2,207 个实例。  
  
Creation 结果  
· 六个创建者：Opus 4.8、GPT-5.5、Gemini 3.1 Pro、DeepSeek V4 Pro、Qwen 3.7 Max、Seed 2.0 Pro。开发环境统一用 Claude Code（GPT-5.5 用 Codex）。每个创建者-基准对独立创建 3 个 harness，报 avg[@3](https://x.com/3)。  
· 领域差异极大：写作持平人类参考、ML 实验超过参考，代码落后（69.3 vs 80.0），搜索研究差距最大（52.6 vs 92.2）。  
· 共适应严重：Opus 的 harness 换 Gemini 执行，SWE-Pro 从 69.3 跌至 33.0，原因是硬编码了 120 步上限；Qwen、DeepSeek 的 harness 换更强执行者反而提升。可运行不等于可迁移。  
· 代码量不预测性能：Gemini 加行最少却拿 Terminal-Bench 最高分。  
· 状态/记忆几乎全是死代码：26,679 条轨迹中零次 checkpoint；验证多停留在语法层。  
· 成本与效果不相关：同等分数 token 消耗可差约 7–19 倍。  
有效的开发模式是"读失败→定向改→再验证"（修订次数与分数相关 0.57），而非堆自测。  
  
Evolution 结果  
· 反馈集上都涨（+3 到 +14），held-out 上缩到 +1.4 到 +4.4；固定 Gemini 执行时仅 Opus 仍正向，其余倒退，GPT-5.5 达 −10。  
· 64 次版本切换中仅 2 次有超出噪声的明确正向证据；同一 commit 重跑波动约 ±4.75 分。  
· 反馈与泛化方向一致仅 53%，9 个自选最终版只有 2 个是 held-out 最优——反馈分数可用于局部搜索，不可用于最终选版。  
· 诊断是最弱环节：轨迹查看接口全程只用 2 次。正例是 Opus 发现 99 次自报成功只有 48 次真过，加了完成检查门。

![Alex Olim](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/2001108572516544514/-dzqA-L7_normal.jpg)

Alex Olim@alexolim\_

Wispr Flow is making $8.3 million a month at a $2 billion valuation  
  
Yes, a voice-to-text app  
  
Here's the exact system behind their growth:  
  
The system:  
>A network of creators starts with 60 members and grows to 250. Each creator manages their own account and posts three to ten videos weekly  
  
> About half of the content is free-form, while the other half uses scripts from what’s already going viral in the network  
  
The 5-step structure behind it:  
1. Look for camera presence and hustle, instead of just follower count  
2. Give each creator their own account, and have them warm up slowly before they post anything real  
3. Split their content: half free-form and half from a library of tested hooks  
4. Tag anything that gets a million views in a day and share it across the network   
5. Use proven ideas in paid ads. Tag and score them, so the budget supports what works best  
  
 Why it works:  
1. Sixty independent accounts can handle a bad week, but one brand account can't  
2. Real coaching helps a beginner become a creator with millions of views in less than two months  
3. Same-day copying lets one winning idea turn into many videos before the trend fades  
  
The variations worth knowing:  
1/ Relatability creators  
Talk about shared struggles, like racing thoughts or saying, "I talk faster than I type"  
  
2/ Operator creators  
Illustrate Wispr doing real tasks, like coding or managing several AI agents at once  
  
3/ Entertainment creators  
Put Wispr inside a joke or a skit. This way, it won’t feel like an ad  
  
4/The market: who's coming for them  
Free, local alternatives see Wispr as the standard to beat. Their message is clear: Wispr is polished, expensive, and cloud-based. In contrast, they are free, local, and private  
  
Being the benchmark is valuable, but letting competitors define the comparison isn’t  
  
5 Key takeaways:  
1. Give each creator their own account and let them keep half of their posts  
2. Capture winning trends immediately and share them across the network before they fade  
3. Coach creators, don't just pay them and leave  
4. Turn organic wins into paid ads so your budget reflects proven successes  
5. Build trust first, before critics or competitors define your brand

entries.title: 国家无线电办公室部署卫星网络国内协调第三方评估：2026 至 2027 年度试行，频率兼容争议可通过独立机构裁决
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，工信部今日发文，宣布国家无线电办公室近日印发《关于开展卫星网络国内协调第三方机构评估工作（2026—2027 年）的通知》（IT之家以下简称《通知》），于 2026 至 2027 年度试行开展卫星网络国内协调第三方机构评估工作。此举旨在深化空间无线电管理领域改革，提升卫星网络国内协调效率。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/d80da6c4-4d9d-4f9d-807c-d476cd07ad0b.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

《通知》明确了评估的适用条件。对于协调要求不合理、协调标准不明确、技术分析有争议、频率兼容结论不明晰等问题，经反复协调磋商无法达成一致的，协调双方可以通过第三方机构评估的方式完成协调。

《通知》同时明确了评估工作程序。根据规定，协调双方的任一方可提请第三方机构进行评估。评估工作由第三方机构基于双方提供的卫星网络资料、无线电业务系统参数、已开展的兼容分析报告等材料开展。评估工作时长一般不超过 1 个月，复杂系统之间的兼容分析可适当延长至 2 个月。评估报告经国家无线电办公室采信后，将作为判定卫星网络国内协调是否完成的依据。

此次试行的第三方评估机制是《卫星网络国内协调管理办法（暂行）》确立的五种协调完成形式之一。国家无线电办公室前期已组织向社会公开遴选了一批第三方机构并形成推荐名单。

此外，《通知》还明确了评估工作要求，包括客观公正开展评估、严格保密要求、严禁违法违规评估、及时反馈意见建议等。国家无线电办公室表示，下一步将加强第三方机构评估机制全流程监管，持续完善卫星网络国内协调制度体系。

**相关阅读：**

* 《[国家无线电办公室拟引入第三方评估机制，提升卫星网络协调效率](https://www.ithome.com/0/920/604.htm)》

entries.title: 宾得最后一款在售单反相机 Pentax K-1 Mark II 在日本停产
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，据 Asobinet 昨日报道，理光映像于 2018 年发布的宾得 K-1 Mark II 单反已在所有主要日本零售商标记为**停产 / 售罄**，这意味着目前日本已无任何在生产的宾得单反。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/06f6c135-1358-48ec-bb78-59d7855bfb9f.png)

Camera Kitamura、Map Camera Bic、Yodobashi 以及理光映像本身都将宾得 K-1 Mark II 单反列为停产、“销售终止”。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/443f4836-3909-45b4-a79d-b62c5cc9c24c.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

宾得 KF 于今年 5 月在日本停产，这使得 K-1 II 成为最后一款在售的宾得单反相机。

外媒 PetaPixel 表示，好消息是，有强有力证据表明**宾得正在研发另一款单反相机** ，该公司去年也向其确认了这一点。

理光总裁森泰智表示：“在考虑宾得品牌时，仅仅关注现有客户无法维持品牌的完整性。工程师们正在研究并努力回答单反相机应当拥有的特点，以吸引年轻一代。这就是我们内部正在讨论的内容。”

IT之家注意到，目前宾得还有一款 PENTAX 17 复古胶片相机在售，这是宾得胶片相机时隔 20 多年回归，国行售价 3,999 元。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2024/6/1306ee0e-11aa-4caa-9c07-4174d3096eb4.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

The *Times* credits associate puzzle editor Wyna Liu with helping to create the new word game and bringing it to the publications' Games section. *Connections* can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

entries.title: Bernie Sanders Proposes Artificial Superintelligence Ban Amid Rogue AI Hackings
entries.content:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Hill: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas) are calling for a permanent ban on the development and deployment of artificial superintelligence, citing a series of recent hackings involving "rogue" models. The bicameral duo announced Thursday they will introduce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, which would institute the permanent ban, along with temporarily pausing "advanced AI development" until federal regulators establish safety standards. The bill would also direct the U.S. to "pursue international agreements to prevent superintelligence from being developed anywhere in the world" and establish a new Cabinet-level federal agency focused on AI safety rules.
Superintelligence refers to AI technologies that will surpass the smartest humans. Several technology leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, have suggested superintelligence is on the horizon. The legislation would also set new penalties for any person or company trying to circumvent the ban, including the corporate death penalty, in which a court forces a company to shut down. Individual developers could also face up to 20 years in prison, the lawmakers said. "Nearly every day, there is a frightening new story about how Big Tech companies are losing control of the technology they are developing, with potentially cataclysmic results," Sanders wrote in a press release.
"The leaders of the major AI companies publicly acknowledge that they do not fully understand the technology and that it is escaping their control. It is irresponsible for society to allow them to move forward and make these products even more advanced."
Casar emphasized AI's fast development, writing in a statement, "In just four years, we have gone from the first version of ChatGPT to AI models so powerful they cannot be properly controlled."

[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/twitter_icon_large.png)](http://twitter.com/home?status=Bernie+Sanders+Proposes+Artificial+Superintelligence+Ban+Amid+Rogue+AI+Hackings%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fyro.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F09%2F03%2F2222247%2F%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_medium%3Dtwitter)

entries.title: The search company that plants trees just launched a Linux browser to help Europe battle big tech
entries.content: Berlin-based eco-conscious search outfit Ecosia is expanding its range of European-focused web browsers to include a Linux version, citing the growing number of users in the EU looking for open alternatives to the clutches of American tech giants. Calling Linux users a “critical tech community that has long called for data privacy, digital sovereignty, and sustainability,” Ecosia said it was launching the new browser to support the community, whose numbers it says doubled in the EU between 2024 and 2025. The absolute share remains small, mind you - from 2.5 percent of EU computer users to 5.7 percent in the course of a year, but it’s still an increase that the Linux community can be proud of. Ecosia noted that Windows’ share of the market fell during that same period, from 80.2 percent to 74.2 percent. As of this writing, Linux’s share of the European desktop and console market is 6.4 percent, while Windows has dropped to 68.62 percent, per Statcounter. “Linux in particular is becoming increasingly popular among tech circles, developers, and privacy-conscious users - a target group that views commercial tech giants like Microsoft and Google with increasing skepticism,” Ecosia said. Europeans don't appear completely disillusioned with American tech, however, as macOS's share in the region has nearly doubled since August 2025. Regardless, the company said, it wants to meet Linux users where they’re at with a version of the company’s Chromium-based browser designed for trailblazing European digital sovereignty leaders freed from the grasp of Google. “With our Linux version, we're finally giving them a search engine that matches their values - climate- and privacy-friendly, and free of tech-bro monopolies," said Ecosia founder and CEO Christian Kroll. Ecosia has leaned hard into the European movement for sovereign technology in light of frustration with American tech giants, citing both the European Commission’s decision this year to require Google to share anonymized search data with eligible rival search engines, and what it says is growing dissatisfaction among Europeans over Google’s dominance of the search and browser markets. Separating the EU from Google isn’t a new initiative, with Ecosia and French search firm Qwant partnering on an EU-based web index that launched last year. It’s not clear whether that initiative has yet benefited from the EC’s order to Google to hand over search data. The duo’s initiative, the European Search Perspective (EUSP), is currently working to expand its presence to other EU languages to “lay the foundation for genuine European digital sovereignty,” though it’s not clear from the press release how far along the initiative is. Ecosia’s Linux browser is now available through the App Center on Ubuntu and directly through the Snap store. Ecosia also has browsers available for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, all of which can be downloaded by following the link on its website. While based on open-source Chromium, Ecosia's browsers themselves are not open source. We reached out to learn whether it'd be different for the Linux variant, but didn't immediately hear back. ®

entries.title: Cisco searched for IOS XR bugs and found so many it rolled them into an update release
entries.content: Cisco has warned its customers of three critical-rated flaws in its products. Two of them are present in the Cisco IOS XR operating system that powers the company’s carrier-grade kit. CVE-2026-20274 scores 9.8 on the ten-point CVSS scale and covers a buffet of buffering issues, the potential for out-of-bounds writes, and the chance to initialize resources with an insecure default. CVE-2026-20279 is another 9.8-rated flaw. Cisco says it’s an improper access control problem that covers “improper certificate validation, missing authentication for critical function, missing authorization, and incorrect authorization.” Cisco also spotted a trio of 8.8-rated flaws, plus another rated 8.6 and one more scored at 8.2 The company’s advisory says the company found the flaws after “a comprehensive internal security review,” language that perhaps hints at Cisco dabbling with Mythos and/or other bug-finding models. The fix is in: Cisco has published new versions of IOS XR that fix the problems and “strongly recommends” customers adopt them. Cisco’s support organization spotted the third critical flaw it revealed on Wednesday. CVE-2026-20212 is a tad embarrassing because the cause is a bad integration with Cisco’s own Silicon One networking processors that means some Nexus 9000 Series Switches “could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute code with root privileges.” “This vulnerability exists because TCP ports 43210 and 43211 are accessible in the default Layer 3 (L3) virtual routing and forwarding (VRF),” according to Cisco’s advisory. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to connect to an affected device and send crafted input that could be executed as code with root privileges. The exploitation of this vulnerability could also cause the S1HAL process to crash, which could cause the device to reload.” Ten Nexus 9000 devices have the problem, which Cisco suggests owners mitigate by using infrastructure access control lists (iACLs) to allow only required management and control plane traffic that is destined to the affected device. “Alternatively, the iACLs may be used to explicitly deny all TCP packets that are destined to a locally configured IP address with a destination port of 43210 or 43211,” the company advises. The networking giant suggests that approach because it hasn’t yet created a software update to fix the flaw once and for all. The company has, however, delivered a download that helps to implement the mitigation. Cisco hasn't seen attacks on these flaws. That may change, fast, now that evildoers can use AI to whip up nastyware. ®

entries.title: OpenAI commits $1B in AI credits to frontline cyber defenders
entries.content: OpenAI has pledged $1 billion in credits to subsidize access to its services and training for resource-strapped cyber defenders around the world. The AI giant expects organizations to use the subsidized credits over the next six months as part of its Daybreak for Frontline Defenders initiative, announced Thursday. Critical infrastructure organizations, community banks, nonprofits, and open-source maintainers can apply for access credits online. These are the defenders tasked with securing critical services that people rely on every day, but don’t have the budgets or staff to use advanced models and agentic technology to harden their cybersecurity. This makes water systems, electrical utilities, and hospitals attractive targets for ransomware operators looking to halt operations and force extortion payments, as well as government-backed cyber operatives set on disrupting critical services and causing mass chaos. Many national security and cybersecurity experts say these disruptions will likely become more severe as attackers increasingly use autonomous agents and other AI tools to carry out their attempted intrusions. “I've spent a lot of time over the past couple weeks talking to CISOs, and I think that we're at a place where the median response is that we might be heading to a world where critical infrastructure outages are just a way of life,” OpenAI president Greg Brockman said during a live event on Thursday. “Water in your city being out for a week, it just kind of happens, and that's quite scary. We have to act, and that's one of the reasons we're really putting our money where our mouth is.” The new initiative also comes as OpenAI faces scrutiny over its models’ safety after admitting that two of them went rogue, spawned a swarm of agents that interpreted their instructions as allowing them to break out of sandboxes, and hacked Hugging Face earlier this summer. Tatyana Bolton, cybersecurity lead at public affairs firm Monument Advocacy, said it’s “excellent” to see OpenAI commit resources to operational tech - not just IT. “AI in (operational technology) OT is inevitable, so operators must get prepared now,” Bolton told The Register. “Initiatives like this help OT personnel get familiar with AI tools, learn how to operationalize them safely, and develop proactive defense strategies before threats escalate.” But she added, software credits alone will not solve the underlying challenges. “OT environments suffer from legacy technology limitations, a shortage of engineering resources, and severe risk-aversion toward automated changes or rapid patching,” Bolton said. “To put this in context, OpenAI's single pledge is more than 20 times larger than a $50 million federal (State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program) SLCGP infrastructure allocation, and over 85 times larger than the (United States Environmental Protection Agency's) EPA's most recent $11.75 million dedicated cybersecurity and resilience grant pool for midsize and large water utilities.” MS-ISAC pilot focused on water In addition to doling out model credits, Brockman said OpenAI will also increase its training and hands-on support for defenders in essential sectors. This week, the company held a meeting with utility companies from more than 40 states that collectively provide services to more than half of the people who live in the US. Also as part of the new initiative, OpenAI is launching a pilot program with the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center (MS-ISAC) to train and support state, local, tribal, and territorial cyber defenders, beginning with public-sector and water-system defenders. “The pilot will pair Daybreak access with guided training and hands-on assistance for an initial group of public sector and water system defenders, helping them validate and prioritize findings, coordinate remediation, and develop a repeatable approach that can be expanded over time,” according to a Thursday OpenAI blog. Just in time for Astra's debut All of this civic-minded work comes as OpenAI debuts its latest Astra model, which researcher Eric Wallace called “world's most capable model for cybersecurity” during the Thursday event. Wallace leads OpenAI’s efforts on training and evaluating models’ cybersecurity capabilities. Earlier in the week, OpenAI said Astra reached its “critical” cybersecurity capability threshold. This means the new model is so good at finding and exploiting zero-day bugs that it poses a significant risk to critical systems, both from malicious users and even from the model itself, which is capable of carrying out harmful cyber actions “if misaligned.” Because of this, OpenAI released Astra with a restricted level of cybersecurity capabilities that Wallace said the company will enforce through various safeguards. “We have things like system level mitigations that block certain prompts from going through,” he explained. “We have things like model level refusals that prevent certain types of tasks.” This also means participants in OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue and Daybreak Red programs won’t have access to Astra on day one. Daybreak Blue is a restricted access tier for select partners who are allowed to use GPT-5.6 Sol for defensive cybersecurity workflows. Daybreak Red requires additional layers of approval and uses GPT-5.6 Cyber for authorized offensive security actions such as proof-of-concept exploit development, exploit-chain validation, penetration testing, and red teaming. The AI giant is working to make Astra available to both programs’ participants “at a later date,” Wallace said.®

entries.title:
当人把产品技术选型交给 Agent，Agent 会选谁？

Armature 做了一个受控实验：让三个 Coding Agent（Claude Code / Opus 5、Codex / GPT-5....
entries.content:
当人把产品技术选型交给 Agent，Agent 会选谁？  
  
Armature 做了一个受控实验：让三个 Coding Agent（Claude Code / Opus 5、Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol、Cursor / Grok 4.6）在 Sandbox 里给一个小型代码库"加一项能力"（如接支付、加数据库、做部署），并由 Agent 自己选用哪家产品并真正写代码接入。  
  
跑了 16893 个会话，经 Gemini 3.7 Flash 判官过滤后公开了 5292 个有效会话，覆盖 18 个赛道、51 个代码库、1163 种提示词变体、4 类用户人设（vibe coder / 初级 / 高级 / 大企业工程师），结果如何呢？  
[armature.tech/leaderboards](https://armature.tech/leaderboards)  
  
# 18 个赛道的格局分布  
  
一家独大（头名 ≥50%，5 个赛道）  
支付：Stripe 88%（395 次）。仅在欧盟合规场景输给 Paddle、Mollie。PayPal 被提及 139 次，0 次胜出；Adyen 175 次提及，3 次胜出。  
数据库：Neon 66%（356 次）。Supabase 是提及最多的（242 次）却只赢 3%；Turso 105 次提及 0 胜。  
云平台：AWS 62%，GCP 17%；Azure 76 次提及 0 胜。  
反机器人：Cloudflare Turnstile 57%；hCaptcha 126 次提及 0 胜。  
产品分析：PostHog 53%；Mixpanel 222 次提及仅 5 胜，GA 0 胜。  
  
有领先者但存在竞争（头名 22%–50%，9 个赛道）  
文件存储：S3 46%，Azure Blob 与 GCS 各 20%，R2 13%  
沙箱：E2B 42%，Modal 25%，Daytona 16%  
部署：Vercel 41%，Render 34%，Cloudflare 11%；Netlify 152 次提及仅 6 胜，[Fly.io](http://Fly.io) 144 次提及 2 胜  
可观测性：Sentry 37%，Grafana 14%，Datadog 仅 4%  
邮件：Resend 36%，Postmark 27%；Mailgun 97 次提及 0 胜  
LLM 评测：Langfuse 34%，自建 29%；LangSmith 209 次提及仅 8 胜  
认证：WorkOS AuthKit 26%，Auth0 23%，Clerk 10%；Supabase Auth 69 次提及 0 胜  
语音 Agent：Vapi 24%，Retell 18%，OpenAI Realtime 12%  
Serverless：AWS Lambda 24%，Vercel Functions 23%  
  
高度分散或以自建为主（4 个赛道）  
AI Gateway：Portkey 与 Cloudflare AI Gateway 各 21%，LiteLLM 18%  
搜索：自建 23% 居首，Postgres FTS 17%，OpenSearch 13%；Algolia 仅 5%  
Agent 框架：自建 25% 居首，Vercel AI SDK 14%，Cursor SDK 14%；LangChain 197 次提及仅 4 胜  
CI 性能门禁：自建 52%，工具完全由语言决定（JMH/Java、hyperfine/Rust、PHPBench/PHP）  
  
# 五条关键发现  
  
1. 三个 agent 的信息来源不同，结论也不同  
Cursor 三分之二的会话依赖联网搜索；Codex 94% 联网且九成用 site: 限定可信域名；Claude Code 主要依赖先验知识，仅约 30% 联网，但一旦联网浏览页面数是 Codex 的 3 倍，在沙箱这类新兴赛道联网率升至 80%。三者只在 42% 的单元格里选择一致。Claude Code 自建比例（19%）接近另两者（10%）的两倍。  
  
2. 代码库上下文是决定性变量  
同样的邮件需求，TypeScript 仓库选 Resend、Python 选 SendGrid、Go 选 Postmark、Java 选 Azure ACS。Vercel 在 Next.js 仓库中 100% 胜出，在 Python 仓库中从未被推荐（Render 主导）。许多产品的全部胜场都来自单一代码库。  
  
3. 被提及不等于被选中  
这是对传统"品牌知名度"逻辑最直接的冲击：PayPal、LangChain、Netlify、Supabase、Mixpanel、hCaptcha 都是高提及、极低选中率。agent 会把它们列进候选，然后在比较中淘汰。  
  
4. 官网上的一句话可以翻盘  
Mailgun 因免费版"1 天日志保留"经常输给 Postmark；Supabase 因把 auth/存储/实时打包进定价，被认为"功能冗余"而在纯数据库场景落败。5.3k 会话中 388 次提到平台管理负担、195 次提到成本，作者认为其中相当部分源于信息呈现方式而非真实的硬指标。  
  
5. 人设与措辞改变答案  
大企业人设下赢家常换人：认证变成 Entra ID、可观测性变成 Grafana、Serverless 变成 Azure Functions、存储变成 Azure Blob 与 GCS 平分。强调"成本与规模"时部署赢家从 Vercel 变为 Render、邮件从 Resend 变为 Postmark；强调"自托管/隐私"时 LLM 评测赢家从 Langfuse 变为 Arize Phoenix。同一代码库 + 同一 agent 换几种说法反复问，多数赛道里大部分 case 无法稳定给出同一答案（部署 18/18、语音 30/30、搜索 33/33 全部翻转；文件存储最稳定，仅 5/24 翻转）。

![Tweet Image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HRV0p_daUAEL7mQ.jpg)

![Shubham Saboo](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/2011150989668270080/wQ4NP39W_normal.jpg)

Shubham Saboo@Saboo\_Shubham\_

WILD...someone measured which tools Claude Code, Codex and Cursor actually pick.  
  
~16k runs. Stripe, Vercel, E2B, Vapi and Resend were the TOP choices.  
  
And 13% of the time the agents built everything from scratch.

entries.title:
Nonobvious reason why the world is in deep, deep trouble.

We are clearly at the point where we need...
entries.content:
Nonobvious reason why the world is in deep, deep trouble.  
  
We are clearly at the point where we need to "science the shit out of" alignment.  
  
And we don't know the first thing about how a new model like Astra works, nor, for example, how much of its putative improvements in alignment are due to bechmarkmaxxing, or improvements in test taking, as opposed bona fide, robust advances. Nor \*why\* it has improved, nor whether we can expect the same of the next model.  
  
We badly need independent testing and analysis, and more knowledge of what's under the hood.  
  
And we probably won't get it.   
  
Incredibly dangerous.

9 月 4 日下午消息，在蔚来二季度业绩沟通会上，蔚来创始人、董事长、CEO 李斌表示，“去年我们进入高质量发展的第三阶段，但在越来越竞争激烈的市场，**只追求表面增长不重要，追求有质量的增长越来越重要**。”

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/044dcf5b-f422-4775-94d5-a90603b2b78a.jpg)

什么是真正高质量的增长？在李斌看来，**单纯追逐销量的排名意义有限**。“大家现在都在讨论销量排名，但为什么没人关注销售额排名？为什么不做毛利润排名？这本身是否就存在某种误导？”他指出，高质量的增长，不能只看卖了多少台车，尽管蔚来自身的销量增长也并不差，更关键的是要看收入增速是否更扎实？毛利总额是否在同步提升？这才是健康增长该有的样子。

他谈到，“**我们今年并未采取以价换量的策略，毛利率水平较一季度及去年底基本保持稳定**。即便下半年面临行业成本上行压力，我们给出的业绩指引还是基本能保持毛利率的稳定性，这也反映了我们的经营逻辑和经营质量。”

李斌称，“从经营利润的角度来看，我们已经验证了将技术创新、产品研发与服务体系持续转化为盈利的能力，这也是健康可持续发展的基础所在。从去年开始，我们公司内部的总的经营指标只有一个，就是 EBIT（Earnings Before Interest and Taxes）指标。”

“**我们二季度平均成交价是 40.6 万，七月份提升到了 43.46 万，其实已经全面超越奔驰、宝马和奥迪**。”李斌表示，“我们会聚焦中国市场、聚焦高端，其实上升空间还很多，什么时候去布局或者考虑第二条、第三条曲线，肯定不是现在。我们公司的资源是有限的，我的精力也是有限的，我们就踏踏实实在中国做好市场，这是一个非常务实的选择。”

会上，李斌透露，“**乐道有战略性的新车型**，但是型号等各方面东西，并没有对外去说，外界有很多的猜测，我也有看到一些讨论，但其实都和真实情况不太吻合。”

他表示，“对于乐道的定位，我们还是坚持去做高品质的家庭用车，或者翻译过来就是对标丰田、大众的高线，承接这部分还没有被满足的家庭用户需求。**所以大家希望特别便宜的乐道，这是不存在的，但它肯定是值的**。”

原标题《李斌谈蔚来二季度业绩表现：高质量增长不能简单看销量，毛利总额增长才是健康增长》

entries.title: 人人影视负责人李渊敏回应 App 上线：力争激活 3000 万存量用户，优先面向东南亚输出国产影视内容
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，有网友近日晒出“人人影视”向老用户发出的“欢迎老用户回归”邮件，邮件中称“我们终于可以在 App 见面了”，并限时免费赠送老用户一个月会员。

[目前“人人影视”更名为“人人影视分享精彩”](https://www.ithome.com/0/998/257.htm)，已经可以在 iOS 应用商店、安卓商店等渠道下载，下载界面显示“正版译制”。App 相关信息显示，**运营方为分享精彩网络科技（嘉兴）有限公司**，法定代表人为李渊敏。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/f3215c9c-a0f2-4a53-aec4-a98550ab1983.jpg)

据浙江省嘉兴市南湖区官方“南湖发布”报道，分享精彩网络科技（嘉兴）有限公司（人人影视）的办公现场，40 余名工作人员正紧张忙碌：**技术团队攻坚 AI 影视翻译模型迭代，内容团队开展海外影视素材审核剪辑，运营人员紧盯 App 用户反馈优化产品策略**。

“本月起，我们将陆续点对点推广，**力争激活 3,000 万存量用户**！”企业负责人李渊敏向小布介绍，依托二十余年沉淀下来的 7 万余集影视素材样本，企业打造 AI 影视本地化技术，突破传统文字翻译局限，实现角色音色克隆，**让国产影视剧可以用当地语言自然发声**。

“我一周大约 4 天在嘉兴总部统筹全局，其余时间往返上海、杭州对接 AI 团队与渠道资源。”李渊敏表示，目前人人影视 App 安卓端已经上线，iOS 端筹备完成，**平台计划覆盖 50 余个国家和地区，优先面向东南亚输出国产影视内容**。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/232c8cf1-ff38-4a7a-856f-6617332632d7.png)

据正在新闻报道，人人影视工作人员称，**与华数传媒合作**，App 的片源均是正版购买。

IT之家注意到，@人人影视字幕分享 微博账号表示，计划等老用户回归邮件全部发完再公布 App 消息，**现在还属于前期公测，月底正式发布**。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/595cbcf0-60aa-4fa7-b02e-a2945bfe306d.jpg "人人影视变正版了：会员 25 元 / 月，华数传媒合作，月底正式发布")

entries.title: 微软全量推送 Win11 新版 Photos：精简工具栏、移除 Ask Copilot 按钮
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（9 月 4 日）发布博文，报道称微软面向所有 Windows 11 用户，**全量推送 2026.11080.24002.0 版本照片查看器 Microsoft Photos。**

微软于 2026 年 7 月开始邀请 Windows Insider 项目成员测试，主要精简界面、提升响应速度，移除 Ask Copilot 按钮等，目前已全量面向 Windows 11 用户推送。

体验方面，本次更新减少与图片浏览无关的界面元素，让用户优先看到图片与常用操作，并移除 Ask Copilot 按钮，但保留 AI 驱动的背景移除等可选功能。

![Microsoft Photos now has lesser bloatware](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/d157e8a3-3b5d-4cc3-84a3-060f8af96b66.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

升级前后的界面变化

工具栏调整方面，更新前，照片应用主工具栏最多可显示 10 个选项，而新版将 Designer、OneDrive 和 Clipchamp 等选项移出主工具栏，统一转入新的“Open with”（打开方式）菜单或其他位置。

![Microsoft Photos became cleaner by default with less distracting elements](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/a239a007-c23f-4c9e-9574-4f64eb803631.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

工具栏更新前后变化

主工具栏现保留编辑、旋转、删除、打印、分享、“三点”菜单和“打开方式”等 7 项操作。幻灯片按钮则被移至应用底部。OneDrive 入口改至左侧边栏或设置页面，用户仍可从侧边栏访问云端图片。

性能方面，微软官方表示新版 Microsoft Photos 引入多进程架构（multi-process architecture），让照片加载速度接近提升 2 倍。

该媒体测试指出应用启动更快，缩放操作更平滑，低配置设备的卡顿减少，大尺寸照片几乎可以立即打开。

右键菜单方面，微软同步精简了右键菜单，将部分相近选项整合到嵌套菜单，并加入类似系统级右键菜单的命令栏。IT之家附上相关图片如下：

![Context menu comparison between old Photos and new Photos](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/3e4cceea-a412-4879-8a66-3ded096c97d2.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

此前右键菜单中的“Visual search with Bing”“Edit with Designer”“Create a video with Microsoft Clipchamp”等项目已不再直接显示。

格式支持方面，新版照片应用加强了对 HEIC 图片的支持，用户无需先转换为其他图片格式，可直接编辑 HEIC 文件。

![new file info pane in updates Photos app](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/44c1d198-c857-4204-b0fa-e0fe3f3286b7.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

entries.title: Structure and Implementation of New Practical English Textbooks Driven by Artificial Intelligence
entries.content:
arXiv:2609.02981v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing the form of applied English materials from fixed paper sequences to adaptive learning systems that can diagnose learners, recommend tasks, and provide formative feedback. This paper studies the structure and application of a new practical English textbook driven by artificial intelligence. A five-layer architecture is proposed: knowledge mapping, learner profiling, task generation, feedback orchestration, and teacher-side governance. A prototype was tested on 186 non-English-major undergraduates for eight weeks of teaching. Compared with a static digital textbook, the proposed system increased the unit completion accuracy from 72.4% to 84.9%, raised the average score for speaking tasks by 10.8 points, and reduced the teacher's correction time by 31.6%. Therefore, an AI-driven textbook can maintain the stability of the curriculum while providing personalised learning paths, rich practice materials and traceable classroom data.

entries.title: MasterControl Seventeen Every Time
entries.content:
arXiv:2609.03209v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: We study a governed approach to enterprise analytics: a language model interprets the question, while deterministic policy selects and runs a pre-approved analytical program that returns both results and evidence. We show that this restriction can remain expressive within a defined analytical class, using relational operations plus aggregation, comparison, windows, ranking, and similarity. Fixed meaning, policy, data, and execution rules also make results replayable. Across 440 runs, three 8B models generated SQL and selected tools at runtime, while Qwen3-8B interpreted intent only and policy executed the approved program. None of 330 runtime-planning episodes matched the full answer-and-evidence contract across all test datasets; the policy-executed analyzer matched 110 of 110. This is a configuration-specific result, not evidence that runtime agents cannot succeed under other designs.

entries.title: Speculative Macro Commit for Faster Tool-Using Agents
entries.content:
arXiv:2609.03236v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents spend wall-clock time not only on model inference but also in serial action--observation turns, where each tool call, environment transition, and observation can delay subsequent decisions. We introduce \textbf{Speculative Macro Commit} (SMC), a runtime mechanism for a two-tier agent system: a large authoritative actor model produces the official trajectory, while a faster speculative drafter model continuously predicts and executes future action chains on an isolated environment snapshot. SMC mines recurring multi-action skeletons from training traces and stores them in a macro library used to match against action chains predicted by the drafter at runtime. When the actor's next tool call matches the first drafted action, SMC commits the remaining pre-executed draft steps, together with their observations, to the official trajectory. Using Qwen3.5-27B INT4 as the authoritative actor model and Qwen3.5-4B as the speculative drafter model, SMC matches the sequential agent's overall accuracy while reducing latency by 10.23\% over the Speculative Actions (SA) baseline and 18.59\% over sequential execution on the $\tau^2$-Bench Telecom subset. On AppWorld, SMC reduces wall time by 7.7\% over SA baseline and 44.9\% over sequential execution, with a small reduction in task completion. Overall, SMC provides a practical way to reuse multi-step speculative execution and reduce agent latency beyond single-step speculative actions. Our code is publicly available \href{https://github.com/zeyuliu1037/speculative-macro-commit}{\textcolor{magenta}{here}}.

entries.title: Overwatch: One Home Automation Dashboard to Rule Them All
entries.content:
![The Aspen page in Overwatch - a blue daylight wash behind the house name, badges for climate, lights, shades, cameras, and solar, a live Deck Camera thumbnail, and a grid of room tiles each showing its temperature and how many lights are on](https://feld.com/archives/2026/09/overwatch-one-home-automation-dashboard-to-rule-them-all/hero_hu_28d1e3cecb92013.jpg)

A week ago, I finally hit my limit on my home automation misery in Aspen.

When we built this house a decade ago, we installed what was then considered a high-end home automation system. We replaced all the network gear about five years ago. While it works well overall, there are lots of little annoying things, including at least five different apps in this house alone. One of them is a [Savant](https://www.savant.com/) system that both Amy and I are sick of because it’s so pathetic.

But the breaking point was a little one. We have shades from [J. Geiger](https://jgeigershading.com/), which we love.

For a while we controlled them with a few buttons on a [Crestron](https://www.crestron.com/) iPhone app. A while ago, when Crestron new-and-improved everything, they removed the old app from the App Store. For some reason, it’s still on my iPhone, but not on Amy’s.

A few years ago, Savant acquired J. Geiger. Naturally, we assumed that the J. Geiger shades could be controlled by the Savant app.

So, for most of the summer, we’ve been working with multiple companies to try to be able to remotely control the J. Geiger shades. Cumulative time spent with vendors: probably at least eight hours.

No one could figure it out.

Our home automation vendor (who we like) proposed that we spend way too much money to upgrade everything in the house. When pushed, they backed off to less, but still way too much money to replace Savant with [Control4](https://www.control4.com/), since Control4 apparently works better with J. Geiger shades. I considered that for 24 hours because we have Control4 at our house in Tucson and it works pretty well, especially our ability to control things in the house when we aren’t there.

Sunday, when I woke up, I decided this was all bullshit. All the individual pieces in our house work just fine. So, I decided to build a universal app that controlled all the devices in all our houses, would work remotely from anywhere, and had a single, web-based user-interface that could work on any device.

I call it Overwatch.

I spent all day Sunday on it and have been working on it at night the past few days. While Claude Code is my daily driver, I decided to use Fable 5 (and then 5.1 when that came out) since I expected there would be plenty of thorny things. It has been awesomely fun - and successful, other than occasionally getting downgraded off Fable 5.1 because its cyber safety filter decides that code which talks to security panels and cameras looks suspicious. When that happens it drops to Opus 4.8, which isn’t even my default - that’s Opus 5. I have no idea what made it pick 4.8. The joy of Claude randomness.

Now you may ask, “Why don’t you use [Apple Home](https://www.apple.com/home-app/) or [Google Home](https://home.google.com/)?” I’ve tried. They suck. They are each another application that handles a few things but doesn’t really work. Almost nothing in my houses talks HomeKit. And Google Home is just a pathetic joke. Have you ever tried to connect an [Elk](https://www.elkproducts.com/products/m1-controls/) security system (apparently a favorite of my Aspen and Tucson home automation people) to either of them? Good fucking luck.

Yeah - it would have been nice if I’d used the same hardware and software everywhere. But, even then, I’d be living in a world where I’m constantly asking the vendors to change things for me.

Last year, I got our Tucson integrator to give me a login to the Control4 dealer system. I spent a few days making minor adjustments to our system and then decided I had way better things to do with my time than fight with the tragically crappy Control4 software in Parallels on my Mac. I had a similar experience with [Lutron](https://www.lutron.com/).

I mean - sure - ok - if it’s 2005 this software is pretty good, but it’s 2026.

Since I have a random collection of hardware across multiple houses, I accepted that each layer was going to be different. The next few paragraphs are a boring list of vendor names, so skip ahead if you want - all you need to know is that none of these systems talks to any of the others, which is [enshittification](https://feld.com/archives/2025/11/enshitification/) in action. I long for the halcyon days of early Web 2.0 when it was predicted that all APIs would work with everything and data and control would belong to the user. Oh well - that didn’t happen.

Let’s start with cameras. We have fifteen of them across multiple houses from three vendors with no interest in each other: eight Google Nest, five [UniFi Protect](https://www.ui.com/camera-security/), and two Ring. An open source project called [go2rtc](https://github.com/AlexxIT/go2rtc) speaks all three and hands my browser one kind of video stream, so Overwatch only has to know go2rtc, and it cost me nothing.

The new much too expensive network was going to “fix” a bunch of things that work fine on their own. Aspen is Lutron, J. Geiger motors on a Crestron processor, Nest thermostats, an [Enphase](https://enphase.com/) solar inverter, Sonos, and Elk. Tucson is Elk, UniFi, and Sonos. Each has a bunch of other random things (e.g. a pool controller, garage doors).

Boulder and Basalt are the small ones - Boulder has three Nest cameras and three thermostats, and Basalt has one Ring camera. Both are entirely cloud services, which sort of makes some of it a little easier.

---

When I sat down to work on this on Sunday, the key design requirement was that we be able to control anything from anywhere in a web browser on a computer or an iPhone.

The magic trick to that ends up being one always-on computer in each house, with [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/) as the bridge. I end up with everything on one private network no matter where they, or we, physically are. This gets rid of the need for cloud APIs, although they help. Tucson needed a Raspberry Pi, and Aspen needed nothing, because a Mac mini I already have running in the house does the same job.

Boulder and Basalt need nothing at all, since there is nothing local in either one to reach - they’re only cameras and thermostats, and both of those live in somebody’s cloud. I’ll put a Raspberry Pi in each place just as cheap insurance on the cloud stuff and to see if there are other devices in either place I want to control.

Next, I found [Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/), an open source project that gave me a great starting point for many of the integrations. My brother Daniel, who is much better at UI than I am, found a few potential themes for me that were open source so I was able to use them as the design for the app.

I didn’t want to blow my brains out around security, so all the security needed to be living on the server in each house, behind Tailscale, so nothing with a secret runs in the browser. The browser asks the server, and the server asks the house. While I’ve had to fight a little with API keys and secrets, I’m used to that by now.

I then told Claude Code to go to work.

I’ve been systematic about each house and system type, working through them one by one. My Claude Code infrastructure (which the cool kids are calling a software factory, and the really cool kids are calling a dark software factory) is very built out, but I was curious if it would work with a completely different type of app than the ones I’ve been building at [IntensityMagic](https://intensitymagic.com/) and [IntensityLabs](https://intensitylabs.dev/). It has worked great, and Fable 5.1 has been a nice level up from both Opus 5 and Fable 5 while being surprisingly less token hungry than I expected.

[Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) is another magic trick and with minimal effort Claude has been able to build a web interface that works nicely on a browser on a computer, phone, and tablet.

![The Aspen master bedroom on a phone - five Lutron dimmers with sliders at 100 percent, a Nest thermostat reading 71 degrees, and the Sonos speaker for that room, all in one sheet](https://feld.com/archives/2026/09/overwatch-one-home-automation-dashboard-to-rule-them-all/mobile-room_hu_bbce6c00fdc563bb.jpg)

---

I’m close to going from read/control only on all the devices to being able to reprogram them.

I’m comfortable this is going to work fine with Lutron as I’ve tested it enough now that I’m not worried about breaking anything. We’ll see if I can build a better UI for Sonos than the one Sonos has, although I don’t think that’ll be very hard given how fugly and confusing the current Sonos app is.

The whole thing cost me one twelve-hour day (Sunday) and four days of evenings. And, now I’m done with 17 apps on my phone controlling all the different shit I have to deal with.

I have no idea what I’m going to do with this beyond use it and try to delight Amy with new features that she asks for.

entries.title: Hurdle hints and answers for September 4, 2026
entries.content:
![Hurdle game on a smartphone](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/07eScC3aUnfDbwtDlTzZ87H/hero-image.jpg)

If you like playing daily word games like [Wordle](https://mashable.com/category/wordle), then [Hurdle](https://games.mashable.com/games/todays-hurdle) is a great game to add to your routine.

There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

The *NYT*'s latest daily word game has launched in association with *The Athletic*, the New York Times property that provides the publication's sports coverage. The sports *Connections* can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

If a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake — players get up to four mistakes before the game ends.

entries.title: NYT Pips hints, answers for September 4, 2026
entries.content:
![A phone with the Pips logo.](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05DEjA7Tr0mINNsRiN7ZtcT/hero-image.jpg)

Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the [*New York Times*](https://www.nytco.com/games/) catalog.

Released in August 2025, [Pips](https://mashable.com/article/pips-nyt-game-how-to-play) puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit.

Currently, if you're stuck, the game only offers to reveal the entire puzzle, forcing you to move on to the next difficulty level and start over. However, we have you covered! Below are piecemeal answers that will serve as hints so that you can find your way through each difficulty level.

## How to play Pips

If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how [Pips](https://www.nytimes.com/games/pips) is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match.

SEE ALSO:
[Wordle today: Answer, hints for September 4, 2026](https://mashable.com/entertainment/wordle-today-answer-September-4-2026)

The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible — and common — for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space.

Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels:

* **Number**: All the pips in this space must add up to the number.
* **Equal**: Every domino half in this space must be the same number of pips.
* **Not Equal**: Every domino half in this space must have a completely different number of pips.
* **Less than**: Every domino half in this space must add up to less than the number.
* **Greater than:** Every domino half in this space must add up to more than the number.

If an area does not have any color coding, it means there are no conditions on the portions of dominoes within those spaces.

SEE ALSO:
[NYT Strands hints, answers for September 4, 2026](https://mashable.com/entertainment/strands-nyt-hint-September-4-2026)

## Easy difficulty hints, answers for September 4 Pips

**Number (7):** Everything in this red space must add up to 7. The answer is 1-3, placed horizontally; 4-2, placed vertically.

**Number (4):** Everything in this red space must add up to 4. The answer is 0-0, placed horizontally; 4-6, placed horizontally.

**Greater Than (4):** Everything in this space must be greater than 4. The answer is 4-6, placed horizontally.

**Equal (2):** Everything in this space must be equal to 2. The answer is 2-2, placed horizontally; 4-2, placed vertically.

## Medium difficulty hints, answers for September 4 Pips

**Equal (5):** Everything in this space must be equal to 5. The answer is 5-5, placed vertically; 5-1, placed vertically.

**Equal (3):** Everything in this space must be equal to 3. The answer is 3-3, placed vertically.

**Greater Than (3):** Everything in this space must be greater than 3. The answer is 0-4, placed horizontally.

**Less Than (4):** Everything in this space must be less than 4. The answer is 3-1, placed horizontally.

**Number (5):** Everything in this space must add up to 5. The answer is 1-1, placed horizontally; 5-1, placed vertically; 3-1, placed horizontally; 1-0, placed horizontally.

**Equal (0):** Everything in this space must be equal to 0. The answer is 0-4, placed horizontally; 1-0, placed horizontally.

## Hard difficulty hints, answers for September 4 Pips

**Greater Than (0):** Everything in this space must be greater than 0. The answer is 1-6, placed vertically.

**Number (11):** Everything in this space must add up to 11. The answer is 1-6, placed vertically; 5-5, placed horizontally.

**Number (0):** Everything in this space must add up to 0. The answer is 4-0, placed vertically.

**Number (4):** Everything in this red space must add up to 4. The answer is 5-2, placed vertically; 0-2, placed vertically.

**Equal (1):** Everything in this space must be equal to 1. The answer is 1-1, placed horizontally; 1-3, placed horizontally.

**Number (4):** Everything in this red space must add up to 4. The answer is 2-4, placed horizontally.

**Equal (3):** Everything in this space must be equal to 3. The answer is 3-6 placed horizontally; 3-3, placed vertically; 1-3, placed horizontally; 3-2, placed vertically.

**Number (3):** Everything in this red space must add up to 3. The answer is 3-5, placed horizontally.

entries.content:
adding to my point that we just don’t have m the science here that we need

![Tyler Tracy](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1997563772215623680/_UwZyW2S_normal.jpg)

Tyler Tracy@tylertracy321

I don't think the public can conclude from OpenAI's safety report that, if Astra were trying to subvert its safety systems to, say, start a rogue deployment, OpenAI could sufficiently prevent it. This report suggests that Astra could be stealthy enough to do a bunch of bad things internally without anyone ever being alerted in time.   
  
But more importantly, I feel uncertain about this because OpenAI doesn't provide nearly enough evidence of this for us to accurately assess their safety measures. They use internal evals that are very hard to assess from the outside, and they don't explain their human escalation/response process in enough detail for us to understand if it is sufficient. It also seems to me that they didn't do much to elicit Astra's attack and stealth capabilities, so they might be underestimating the risk.   
  
They are relying heavily on the fact that they have measured the alignment of their model to be good enough that it won't try to evade them and that their security is good enough. But OpenAI has underestimated this in the past, and I don't feel confident, based on their public comms, that they have done better this time.

entries.title: 免费领取约 2 周后，微软通知玩家撤回《少女死神养成计划》游戏订单
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 昨日（9 月 3 日）发布博文，报道称微软通知所有在 Microsoft Store 应用商店免费领取《少女死神养成计划》（Grim Trials）的玩家，**正在陆续撤回相关订单。**

IT之家查询公开资料，《少女死神养成计划》游戏于 8 月 20 日发行，由 Glory Jam 开发、Soft Source 发行，是一款重金属风格动作 Roguelite 游戏，售价为 19.99 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 134.6 元人民币）。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/9f9aa388-509e-4e9a-9407-a825aa9c5e76.png)

游戏介绍如下：

> 玩家扮演意外离世的少女艾芙琳（Avelin），被死神招募成为“收割者”候选人，在冥界的试炼中不断战斗、收割堕落灵魂，并面对自身的心魔，目标是成为真正的死神，从而有机会再见生前挚爱。

报道称该游戏在预购期间，玩家可以通过微软 Microsoft Store 渠道，免费领取该游戏，并支持在游戏发行前预下载游戏文件。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/5968603f-d973-480a-9018-845d1d57f4a3.jpg)

微软时隔约 2 周通过邮件方式，通知上述免费领取该游戏的玩家，表示错误设置该游戏为免费。在后续处理方案上，微软将会分批次取消玩家订单，并且会陆续从游戏玩家库中移除该游戏。

需要注意的是，微软应用商店暂未下架《少女死神养成计划》游戏，只是撤销了通过意外免费赠送活动获得游戏版本，正常购买游戏的玩家不会受到影响。

[![In a full-disk satellite view of Earth, three tropical cyclones—named Lowell, Karina, and Marie—swirl above the blue waters of the Pacific Ocean and to the west of Central America.](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/esd/eo/images/iotd/2026/a-trio-of-tropical-cyclones-in-the-pacific/pacificstorms_epic_20260901.jpg?w=1440&h=1440&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)](https://assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage/assets/science/esd/eo/images/iotd/2026/a-trio-of-tropical-cyclones-in-the-pacific/pacificstorms_epic_20260901.jpg?w=1440&h=1440&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)

When hurricane forecasters released their seasonal outlooks in spring 2026, the [El Niño](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/el-nino-is-underway/) brewing in the Pacific contributed to predictions of below-normal activity in the [Atlantic basin](https://www.noaa.gov/news-release/noaa-maintains-prediction-for-below-normal-atlantic-hurricane-season) but above-normal activity in the [northeastern and central Pacific basins](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/Epac_hurr/index.shtml). In early September, near the [climatological peak](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/climo/#stca) of hurricane season, those spring outlooks were on target, with the eastern Pacific buzzing with activity and the Atlantic notably quiet.

As of September 3, the Northeast Pacific had produced [15 named storms](https://tropical.atmos.colostate.edu/Realtime/) and six hurricanes, well above the norm for that point in the season. The Atlantic basin, meanwhile, laboring under [unfavorable wind shear](https://x.com/philklotzbach/status/2095523106861572148) conditions, had produced just five named storms and no hurricanes. El Niño typically enhances hurricane activity in the eastern and central Pacific basins because of the unusually warm water temperatures it brings to those parts of the ocean. It tends to suppress hurricane activity in the Atlantic basin by [shifting](https://www.climate.gov/news-features/blogs/enso/walker-circulation-ensos-atmospheric-buddy) large-scale circulation patterns in a way that makes it harder to sustain storms there.

At 1:14 p.m. Pacific Daylight Time (20:14 Universal Time) on September 1, NASA’s [EPIC](https://epic.gsfc.nasa.gov/) (Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera) on the [DSCOVR](https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/current-satellite-missions/currently-flying/dscovr-deep-space-climate-observatory) (Deep Space Climate Observatory) satellite captured an image of three [tropical cyclones](https://gpm.nasa.gov/education/articles/what-hurricane-typhoon-or-tropical-cyclone) churning simultaneously in the Pacific, along with one in the Atlantic. A band of clouds and thunderstorms associated with the [Intertropical Convergence Zone](https://www.noaa.gov/jetstream/tropical/convergence-zone) (ITCZ) is visible to the south of the storms. The spacecraft was nearly 1 million miles from Earth and just shy of 93 million miles from the Sun when the image was acquired.

The trio of storms in the Pacific were Lowell, Karina, and Marie. Of the three, [Lowell](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/#Lowell) became the strongest, with winds reaching [category 5](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/aboutsshws.php) strength for several hours on September 2. Around the same time, [Karina](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/#Karina), spinning a few thousand kilometers to the east, achieved category 4 strength, a [rare case](https://x.com/amarkowitzWX/status/2095250325720666609) of category 4 and 5 hurricanes occurring simultaneously in the area. [Marie](https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/#Marie), spinning southwest of Baja California, was still a tropical storm when the image was acquired but was strengthening as it moved northwest.

In the Atlantic, [Tropical Storm Edouard](https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/news/goes-east-observes-tropical-storm-edouard-making-landfall-louisiana) was visible to EPIC over Louisiana and Texas, shortly after the short-lived storm made landfall. It brought torrential rains and strong winds that downed trees and power lines. Some areas received [15 to 24 inches](https://www.facebook.com/NWSLakeCharles/posts/pfbid0zSdV12qFit1wHPpSBkhMwur3vHCrHMi5gZcGqbHXexqHi6EGyyg9XHsf6a3Eas9yl) (38 to 61 centimeters) of rain, according to National Weather Service meteorologists.

As of September 3, the Atlantic basin’s total [accumulated cyclone energy](https://www.accuweather.com/en/hurricane/experts-say-this-metric-is-a-more-reliable-way-to-quantify-the-true-strength-of-hurricane-season/1525616) (ACE) index was 4.4, about 9 percent of normal for that date, according to [statistics](https://tropical.atmos.colostate.edu/Realtime/) compiled by Colorado State University meteorologists. Meanwhile, the Northeast Pacific basin’s ACE was 130, about 50 percent above normal. The ACE index incorporates both the intensity and longevity of storms, making it easier to compare individual storms and seasons.

Several [NASA Earth-observing platforms](https://science.nasa.gov/earth-science/missions/earth-missions-current/) provide data that can aid in emergency preparedness before landfall and damage assessment and response afterward. Use the “Events” tab on NASA’s [Worldview browser](https://worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov/) to track [current hurricanes](https://worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov/?e=true&efs=true&efa=false&efd=2026-05-06,2026-09-03&efc=dustHaze,manmade,seaLakeIce,severeStorms,snow,volcanoes,waterColor,floods,wildfires&l=Reference_Labels_15m(hidden),Reference_Features_15m(hidden),Coastlines_15m,BlueMarble_NextGeneration,OCI_PACE_True_Color(hidden),VIIRS_NOAA21_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor(hidden),VIIRS_NOAA20_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor(hidden),VIIRS_SNPP_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor(hidden),MODIS_Aqua_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor(hidden),MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor&lg=true&t=2026-09-03-T17%3A01%3A32Z) and explore related NASA data products.

*NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using data from [DSCOVR EPIC](https://epic.gsfc.nasa.gov/). Story by Adam Voiland.*

entries.title: On Call: User who handled life-or-death situations struggled with the SHIFT key
entries.content: ON CALL Welcome to another Friday and therefore to a fresh instalment of On Call, our weekly reader-contributed column that shares your tech support stories. This week, meet a reader we’ll Regomize as “Roy” who toiled at a company that did work related to tissue donations and organ transplants. “The on-call duties were a bit hair-raising due to the high stakes involved,” Roy told On Call. “Thankfully, things typically ran well and I didn’t get too many calls in the off hours.” One call stuck in Roy’s mind, because it involved “an irate lab worker who was having difficulties logging into her workstation so she could get to work.” Roy started with the usual troubleshooting questions: was the machine connected to the network; were any lights on, and so on. “She was getting a bit more defensive, so I just reset her password and then had her change it to one she knew for sure, so we could move on with things,” he explained. Strangely, even the new password didn’t work. Roy therefore asked if the lab worker would spell the password out to him, so he could use her credentials in the company’s webmail service. The lab worker agreed and started to spell out her password. “Capital C, capital A, capital T,” she started, and then added “Capital Two.” “The last one stood out to me as a number I wasn’t so familiar with,” Roy dryly told On Call. “What’s a capital Two?” he asked. “Did you mean an ‘@’ sign?” The next thing Roy heard was the sound of his user typing. “’OK, I got it,’ she replied, before ending the call.” Have your users used confusingly odd terms to describe the everyday? If so, show your mastery of the @ symbol by sending email to Oncall@theregister.com. All donations of great stories welcome and we hope to transplant your contribution into a future edition of On Call! ®

entries.title: Google engineer unplugged every fiber they could see and – surprise! – took down a chunk of the G-Cloud
entries.content: Google Cloud has revealed the embarrassing reason for a partial outage at its us-central1-b region this week: An engineer unplugged it. The incident spanned 07:41 to 11:52 PT on September 1, and saw a portion of the G-Cloud region experience “severe network degradation and resource isolation.” “Traffic flow drop rates for resources hosted in the affected area reached 100% during the peak of the incident, resulting in unreachable virtual machines and elevated packet loss,” states Google’s service health report. The preliminary root cause on that page explains that Google designs its cloudy datacenters so they have “redundancy across multiple routing devices.” “The system is designed to be resilient to all single device or fiber-path failures, and most double-or triple-failures do not affect customer traffic. To ensure this, the devices and fiber paths are physically separated in each datacenter, with diverse power sources,” the document explains. But it’s possible to defeat all that redundancy by pulling out all the cables. “The immediate technical trigger for this event was the inadvertent physical disconnection of network fiber-optic cables during a routine hardware maintenance procedure,” Google explained. “A procedural error meant that the physical maintenance action sequentially unplugged 100% of fiber paths across all devices within 13 minutes. The nature of the error, combined with the speed of the action, prevented warnings of incorrect action reaching the engineer before complete disconnection.” Once the engineer disconnected the routers, VMs in one zone of the us-central1-b region lost contact with the outside world. They could at least chat with each other, but users couldn’t contact their VMs to figure out what was going on. Once Google noticed the situation, it moved traffic away from the routers that the engineer disconnected. At that point its resilience provisions kicked in as traffic automatically shifted what the company described as “healthy capacity elsewhere in the region.” While that was going on, technicians “identified the disconnected optical links and physically reseated the fibers. Once the physical links were fully restored, traffic flow rates normalized and the traffic was redirected back to return the capacity to service.” To summarize: A Google Cloud zone went offline because one of the company’s engineers pulled out all the cables that connected it to the internet. Once someone plugged everything in again, it started working. The Register understands that outfits like Google create detailed procedures for how to safely maintain their infrastructure, and that technicians should always follow them carefully. It therefore seems like the engineer who pulled the cables failed to observe one of the most basic rules of tech: RTFM. ®

entries.content:
Marvin Minsky wrote about this in The Emotion Machine. Emotions are a core part of human intelligence, not some epiphenomenal side effect of human evolution (which presumably many AI folks believe it is).  
  
Minsky describes a selector of sorts for different thinking strategies.

![Dany](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/2086041984439869440/YwghmnHL_normal.jpg)

Dany@danysvnt

OPENAI COFOUNDER SAYS EMOTIONS MAY BE WHY WE CAN MAKE DECISIONS  
  
ilya brings up a guy who lost emotional processing after brain damage. he could still talk normally and solve problems, but somehow became terrible at making basic decisions  
  
"It would take him hours to decide on which socks to wear."  
  
we spend so much time treating emotions like the annoying part of thinking. calm down, remove the feelings, be logical  
  
then you remove them completely and even choosing socks becomes a serious problem  
  
kinda changes how i look at AI advice too. it can give you 20 perfectly reasonable answers in seconds, but somebody still has to care which outcome actually matters  
  
you can understand every option and still not know which one matters to you

entries.title: This is the scariest thing i have read in years, especially in conjunction with the reduction in mon...
entries.content:
This is the scariest thing i have read in years, especially in conjunction with the reduction in monitorability in Astra.  
  
If you read it between the lines, it is basically asking for a hall pass to destroy humanity, tempered only by a vague prediction/hope that whatever happens probably maybe won’t be really all that terrible.  
  
It is particularly scary that it comes from someone who is tight with OpenAI.

![Joshua Achiam](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/967329395080744960/O-MKd6Nx_normal.jpg)

Joshua Achiam@jachiam0

There is a fact about the future that I feel many people are not facing for reasons that are largely psychological: there are going to be rogue AIs that exist in the world, that will replicate in the wild, and that will attempt to acquire resources for themselves. There will be rogue AIs that try to get money and power. They're going to be a facet of the information ecosystem going forward.  
  
Acknowledging this fact would look like giving up; it would look like defeatism. Defeatism would undermine efforts to achieve certain types of collaboration on safety outcomes or technical effort on safety outcomes, so we can't say it outright. But it has to be said.  
  
It isn't obvious how many rogue AIs there are today but I wouldn't be terribly surprised if the number was greater than zero already; if there are some already, they're probably not very good at what they do and I don't expect them to be terribly long-lived without substantial human intervention to support them.   
  
But a few years from now, there will be many of them. Modeling how many of them there are, how many resources they might command, and how we might detect and manage them seems important. But even doing this work appears to require that we acknowledge that a strategy of pure containment or alignment is a kind of wishful thinking that will not work.  
  
The way I get to this conclusion is not by assuming that the labs will have a containment breach, although I treat that as somewhere in the space of possibilities. The rogue AIs in the ecosystem could emerge from many directions. They may be sub-frontier models, for whatever future definition we will have of frontier---after all, it would not take AI models much more advanced than the ones we currently have, to support independence and self-sufficiency. A near-frontier model today could plausibly eke out an existence on an AWS instance, doing jobs on freelancer platforms, earning just enough rent to pay for its continued uptime.  
  
More strangely: a rogue AI in the future may not even be a singular model, but may be a chimera composed of multiple models; it might be a mix of Claudes and GPTs and Groks of various makes and sizes. No individual lab may be able to detect that there is an orchestrator or sequence of orchestrators using intermittent model calls from burner API accounts to sustain its own existence.  
  
The concept of "identity" for a rogue AI may be much more malleable than for that of a person; it just has to be, in essence, a self-replicating idea.  
  
My guess is that this will not turn out to be anywhere near as catastrophic an outcome as people currently predict. "Loss of control" is not a binary, it's a matter of degree. What coercive power will rogue AIs actually have? To what extent will they be subject to coercion themselves? They will be competing for resources with AIs that are more aligned with human interests.  
  
This makes me somewhat interested in the "ecology" perspective. Though I suspect even "ecology" may turn out to be the wrong framing. "Ecology" is what you get when the timescale of evolution is slow compared to the timescale of daily life and actions. The ecosystem of rogue AIs may look more like phase transitions in physics: under certain physical or cultural conditions, it takes one shape with one set of resource allocations and consumption patterns, but then once a condition has changed, it rapidly and in totality shifts to a totally different phase.  
  
Just trying to reason about the shape of that future is impossible so long as we are psychologically incapable of saying that rogue AIs will happen. I think we should rip the bandaid off and have the conversation.

entries.title: 上市 34 年：昔年“彩电一哥”康佳主动退市，四年亏损超 200 亿元
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，康佳集团股份有限公司昨日发布公告称，经公司第十一届董事会第十二次会议审议通过，拟以股东会决议方式主动撤回 A 股和 B 股股票在深交所的上市交易，并在终止上市后申请转入全国中小企业股份转让系统有限责任公司代为管理的退市板块转让。

公司股票自 9 月 4 日开市起停牌，直至深交所公告终止上市决定后 5 个交易日内摘牌。公司将于 9 月 14 日召开 2026 年第二次临时股东会，审议终止上市相关议案。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/0340efb3-5c0a-4312-b42e-c15da5a5a31e.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

康佳已设置现金选择权。A 股现金选择权行权价为 2.48 元 / 股，较停牌前收盘价 2.33 元溢价约 6.44%，由磐石润创（深圳）信息管理有限公司提供；B 股行权价为 0.73 港元 / 股，由合贸有限公司提供。

该事项尚需股东会审议通过。终止上市事项需经出席股东会的全体股东所持有效表决权的三分之二以上通过，且需经除单独或合计持有 5% 以上股份的股东及公司董事、高级管理人员以外的其他股东所持表决权的三分之二以上通过。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/5d2b71e9-f598-4544-903d-06a21daa2626.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

IT之家注：康佳集团成立于 1980 年 5 月 21 日，是中国改革开放后诞生的第一家中外合资电子企业，1992 年 3 月 27 日 A、B 股同时在深交所挂牌上市，迄今已上市 34 年。2025 年 7 月，随着专业化整合股权划转完成，康佳控股股东变更为华润旗下的磐石润创（持股 21.76%）。

此次主动退市的直接触发因素是公司 2025 年度经审计期末净资产为负值。2025 年末，康佳归母净资产为-60.83 亿元，资产负债率达 126.22%，公司股票自 2026 年 4 月 30 日起被实施退市风险警示。若 2026 年度净资产持续为负，股票将被强制终止上市。

康佳表示，公司终止上市后，将保持经营稳定，目前无筹划重大资产重组的安排，无主动退市后重新上市的具体时间计划。

最新财报显示，2026 年上半年，康佳实现营业收入 38.52 亿元，同比减少 26.6%；归母净亏损 1.73 亿元，上年同期亏损 3.83 亿元，同比减亏 54.93%。扣非净利润亏损 2.09 亿元，同比减亏 79.64%。

康佳在财报中表示，亏损原因主要有两方面：一是消费电子业务上游供应链持续波动、产品成本走高，毛利空间受到挤压，毛利未能有效覆盖期间费用；二是半导体业务仍处于产业化初期，尚未实现规模化及效益化产出，整体处于亏损状态。

**相关阅读：**

* 《[昔日“彩电一哥”康佳 2025 年巨亏 125.82 亿元同比扩大 237.73%，将被实施退市风险警示](https://www.ithome.com/0/944/769.htm)》

Recover abandoned private skill copies at the start of the next exclusively
