entries.title: 中国一汽攻克硫化物全固态电池低压力运行重大技术难题，实现 5 兆帕稳定循环
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，中国一汽今日宣布，中国一汽联合东方理工大学，**在硫化物全固态电池低压力运行领域取得重大技术突破**，相关成果以“离子弹性体界面实现低压力高稳定固态电池”为题，发表于国际顶级期刊《Advanced Energy Materials》。

![图片](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/371946e4-9310-4372-9c66-3d0c86bd66c4.jpg)

**全固态电池普遍需要 20 兆帕以上工作压力**，这一长期存在的世界性难题，严重制约了其产业化落地。

针对该瓶颈，中国一汽聚焦低压力工况下界面接触衰减这一核心痛点，通过材料形貌调控、电芯低压结构创新及制备工艺优化，**成功实现大容量全固态电芯在仅 5 兆帕的低压力下稳定循环**。这一突破大幅降低电芯对外部压力的依赖，适配电池包工程化设计，为硫化物全固态电池规模化量产应用提供关键技术基础。

中国一汽表示，这标志着我国在硫化物全固态电池实用化关键核心技术上取得里程碑式突破，为全固态电池产业化进程迈出关键一步。
entries.summary: 中国一汽联合东方理工攻克硫化物固态电池难题，实现5兆帕低压稳定循环。

entries.title: 《羊蹄山之魂》DLC“弦续关原”及新模式“无尽追缉”官宣，10 月 1 日解锁
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，在昨天（3 日）晚间的 State of Play 发布会上，索尼宣布《羊蹄山之魂》全新战斗生存模式“无尽追缉”将加入《对马岛之魂》主角境井仁，并支持玩家直接操作。

索尼和 Sucker Punch 展示了“无尽追缉”的最新内容。该模式提供多名可操作角色，包括《羊蹄山之魂》的笃、长门和雪，以及回归的境井仁。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/bab771a2-3200-4d32-bd39-eedfde02c5ef.jpg)

据IT之家了解，“无尽追缉”将与全新单人剧情 DLC《弦续关原》**一同于 10 月 1 日推出**。玩家需要接受悬赏任务开始每轮挑战，在击败敌人后获得增益，并逐步解锁更多可操作角色。

Sucker Punch 表示，境井仁将成为《羊蹄山之魂：无尽追缉》的可操作角色之一。“我们非常高兴能让《对马岛之魂》的英雄在这个新模式中回归，并完整保留他的 4 种标志性架势。‘无尽追缉’是我们对 Roguelike 玩法的一种诠释。玩家可以从 4 名角色中进行选择，并接受难度不断提升的悬赏任务。完成一轮轮挑战后，玩家可以获得增益和升级，用来强化角色，让实力不断提升。”

Sucker Punch 称，团队非常重视让“无尽追缉”成为《羊蹄山之魂》核心战斗系统的延伸。玩家仍然会使用熟悉的武器和系统，每轮挑战也会带来新的体验，也可以尝试不同角色和配装，找到最适合自己的装备组合。

《弦续关原》则采用双线叙事。索尼介绍称：“剧情将在现代时间线与笃身处日本本土时期的回忆之间展开。玩家将遇见长门，他是笃过去认识的人，随后来到虾夷。现代时间线中，玩家将探索一个此前从未出现过的山谷，那里过去曾是‘蛇’及其忠实追随者‘蝮蛇’的据点。过去的时间线则会让玩家亲历笃参加关原之战的经历，以及她返回故乡踏上复仇之路前人生中的一个关键时刻。扩展内容还将加入新敌人、重型武器、全新铠甲套装和染料等内容。”

entries.title: Molecular snapshots reveal how bacteria assemble outer membrane proteins
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: Gram-negative bacteria are responsible for several infections that are hard to treat because of their high resistance to antibiotics. These bacteria possess an outermost layer called the outer membrane that acts as a protective barrier. Serving as the cell's interface with the outside world, the outer membrane contains specialized proteins that perform multiple functions, such as nutrient transport and environmental sensing. The localization of these outer membrane proteins is achieved through the combined action of several key players, including the SurA chaperone and the β-barrel assembly machinery (BAM) complex.

entries.title: Data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
entries.content:
Battlefields in Ukraine are littered with the remnants of drones, which are now firmly established as a critical weapon of modern warfare. But behind all that wreckage, there’s a new [gold mine](https://www.wired.com/story/ukraine-government-battlefield-data/) for the defense sector. The data drones generate will far outlast the wars in which they are used to fight, increasingly becoming part of the AI architecture that shapes even civilian life.

For every flight, unmanned systems collect thousands of points of data, from images and video to controller inputs. Together, those records show how a machine and a person responded to constantly shifting circumstances.

Ukraine has now begun converting that experience into a resource. Its Ministry of Defense announced in January that it would make millions of data points gathered during tens of thousands of drone flights available to both military contractors and commercial companies, and since then more than [100 companies](https://mod.gov.ua/en/news/over-100-ukrainian-companies-are-already-leveraging-brave1-dataroom-to-train-ai-models) and the [UK government](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/aug/24/uk-to-use-ukraine-battlefield-data-to-train-ai-to-protect-sensitive-sites) have gained access.

For a country at war, it’s a quick way to attract funding and partnerships. But this step turns the front line into an active site of model training, taking advantage of how the chaos of war creates conditions that AI companies struggle to reproduce on their own.

Other countries and battlefields are likely to follow Ukraine’s lead, but the responsibility for governing this new industry cannot fall solely on a country fighting for its survival. That legal vacuum has to be filled together by the countries and companies involved in this industry’s development.

### Explosive growth

Ukraine’s battlefields are not the first to produce records used to train and develop models: American drones over Syria and Yemen collected data that informed the first generation of semiautonomous military hardware in the late 2010s.

The difference now is that access to that data is being used to develop a wider ecosystem. And the financial value to defense firms is immense: Battlefield data offers large volumes of machine experience gathered under conditions that no laboratory can produce.

That’s because the data that’s most valuable for training AI models comes from exceptions: the moment visibility disappears, a signal jams, or a human operator improvises. AI companies spend years and enormous sums trying to capture enough of these moments to make their models more robust. But war produces them at a frequency controlled testing cannot match.

This constantly changing terrain is what makes drone data valuable far beyond the battlefield. A commercial drone used for delivery or remote sensing may never encounter artillery fire, but it must still operate with incomplete information in a world where people behave unpredictably. The same problem is compressed by war into a much shorter timeline.

Processed and matched against records of what its operator was doing, that data turns operational records into training sets. Combat becomes a commercial asset.

Many conflicts have already seen this training loop happen as drone footage feeds subsequent generations of military technology, and the market is set to grow. Enabled Intelligence, an American company that specializes in processing data to become usable in AI training, says it has already made more than [half a million](https://defensescoop.com/2026/06/16/data-from-half-a-million-hours-of-ukraine-conflict-drone-footage-now-available-to-train-ai/) hours of Ukrainian drone footage available to feed into the next round of models, advertising possible uses in both military and commercial systems.

### Closing the data loop

Many of the drones that now define our modern age of warfare began as civilian technology. But they’ve recently been turbocharged by new, commercially available AI systems, which allow cheap machines to operate autonomously—either individually or as a flock—as the environment changes around them. Each flight then creates a record of what the system encountered.

The resulting data is critical. The controlled lab environments usually developed to train these autonomous systems can approximate failure but are no match for  the live conditions of a battlefield with very real risks. Military intelligence programs have held data generated by sensor-heavy systems like Predator and Reaper drones for nearly a decade through programs like Project Maven, but access remained entirely within the defense world. The data generated was available only through restricted, classified channels for the sole purpose of developing new weapons systems that would feed back into the same military that produced the data in the first place. That experience is now being shared to a much broader development network.

The loop now closes. Commercial technologies adapted for the battlefield are generating data that can flow back into the industries from which they came, becoming part of the data infrastructure relied on by governments and the private sector alike.

Drones that were trained in the signal-jammed airspace over Ukraine are now being deployed in the [agricultural sector](https://drone.ua/en/blogs/news/droneua-and-syngenta-agrodrones-in-action-digital-transformation-of-the-ukrainian-agricultural-sector) to help farmers map and survey their fields in places lacking the cell signal necessary for previous generations of technology.

Other countries are likely to follow Ukraine in selling their battlefield data, and we are not ready for the new marketplace this will create.

Bad actors could acquire the data, but purchase controls already mitigate that risk. Intelligence operatives scrutinize potential customers’ infrastructure for ways that data could reach enemies or nefarious actors.

Training data creates a new tracing problem, though. Whereas the movement of commercial datasets can be followed when planted contact details appear two steps from the original buyer, the provenance of AI training data vanishes in a manner embedded in the technology itself. Another risk is that this use of the data creates an extractive economy in which wealthier countries far from danger benefit from the mortal threat borne by frontline states, potentially creating a market incentive for war to continue as an unending mine for digital gold.

### A fraught new frontier

Existing laws regulate how militaries may conduct war. But they say almost nothing about what happens when records created in combat are stripped of their operational context, packaged as data, and licensed to companies whose products circulate far beyond where they were made.

The responsibilities of the companies that design these systems remain unsettled. Ukraine is building access controls, which are mentioned in the newly signed UK-Ukraine AI agreement, but no governments are actively working on regulating what happens when data has been absorbed into a model and crosses back into civilian markets.

Those records contain human lives. The soldiers and civilians visible in them did not agree to become training material for products that might be sold years later. But sensor data, camera footage, and coordinates from civilians fleeing a drone strike now constitute the sorts of data that inform how future machines will make decisions.

That is a problem of consent. Individuals featured in the data—be they targets, controllers, or civilians standing by—become part of the training material. The autonomous capabilities based on that data do not stop at the edge of the battlefield. Such capabilities move into other military or commercial systems like delivery vehicles or agricultural machinery. Errors and assumptions embedded in the data travel with the model even once it enters civilian life.

Battlefield data should not be treated as ordinary commercial material. But there is currently no agency or regulator that has jurisdiction over this issue. In the meantime, governments that provide access to defense data should treat it as they would a controlled weapons transfer, recording its origin, licensing its users, and restricting onward sharing. Ukraine has begun to grapple with this. Its Avengers Labs program allows companies to train models on battlefield data without giving them direct access to sensitive databases. Yet that mitigates only one part of the problem.

Governments should require disclosure when models trained on wartime material are later incorporated into civilian products. The goal of such regulation should be to make the path from combat to commerce visible.

What these companies are really mining is experience. And soldiers cannot consent to having their experience used in this way—as training data that produces model advantage and ultimately supports a product used far from where the war was fought.

The question is no longer only what the technology companies can sell for use in war. It is what they can extract from it.

To protect ourselves from the excesses of this new industry, we need a regulatory system that follows battlefield data wherever it goes, from combat to model to commercial product.

*Cory Alpert is a researcher at the University of Melbourne, looking at the impact of AI on democracy. He previously served in the Biden White House.*

entries.title: feat: enable Swarm by default (#136514)
entries.content:
```
feat: enable Swarm by default (#136514)

* feat: enable Swarm with callable collector capabilities

Enable Swarm by default while preserving explicit global/per-agent opt-outs, existing limits, tool profiles, and Code Mode opt-in. Finalize collector affordances from surviving native readers and retain execution policy through catalog updates; preserve inherited Codex declarations and closure-bound joined spawning.

Include profile, lifecycle, registration and UI regressions. Refresh the explicitly approved single SDK export budget and existing-main communityInvite config count. Context: #136514 and #136472.

* test: align Swarm fixtures with callable tool surfaces

* test: bind collector guidance to callable tool fixtures

* fix(config): preserve authored state across runtime writes

Discard derived deletions for runtime-only fields instead of creating
empty source containers during subsequent settings writes. Preserve
explicit empty objects, live SecretRefs, file defaults, and source intent
across direct and replacement callers.

Carry the resolved precommit source into canonical-reread recovery so
metadata and runtime-only defaults cannot be confused with authored state.

Found during Swarm's Labs opt-out/reset proof (#136514). Regression tests
cover ordered writes, replacement callers, and invalid rereads.

* test: cover Swarm upgrades with preserved Codex catalogs

Document the supported separate ordinary-session path for supervised native catalogs without agents_wait. Preserve existing thread ownership and cover explicit-off metadata followed by omitted-config resume and fresh registration. No runtime behavior changes.

* fix(agents): refresh callable dependencies before catalog reuse

Normalize current reader bindings before descriptor-fingerprint reuse and identical-entry restriction checks. Preserve canonical ordering and immutable descriptor snapshots without allocating a second mapped array. Cover denied, copied, lookalike and unchanged-reader boundaries with real tool factories; four regressions failed before repair.

* fix(ui): coalesce missing avatar requests across renders

Retain settled misses briefly in the existing bounded avatar cache so chat updates do not repeatedly fetch absent photos. Preserve revision and credential invalidation, unversioned recovery, and pending blob lifetimes.

Found during the default-on Swarm live trial for #136514. Five regressions fail before the fix; 154 owner and sibling tests, final focused tests and changed checks, full build, and independent review pass. Fresh live UI proof remains required before landing.

* test(ui): assert cached avatar fallback across rerenders

Replace the obsolete second-request gates with the first completed avatar response and an exact one-request assertion across the real Reply interaction. Preserve initials, fallback, URL, and resource-type checks without increasing timeouts.

The complete file fails against pre-fix avatar behavior with five requests instead of one. All four tests, the original CI shard selector, rebased lifecycle checks, static gates, build, and independent review pass. Completes the remaining UI test repair for #136514.
```

entries.title: OpenAI发布GPT-6 Astra，IFM与MBZUAI开源K2 Horizon六档模型
entries.content:
原创 每日发现最新 2026-09-04 16:32 中国香港

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=164135e2&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FUibyxhuYSuFaha1CXmAqLLFmHZ1giaI5ibgOOddL6ibZd7UkpHf0OmYJ0B1QufSfneadXPJbW0dkniagsd6iaonB78fSJFnbn6yV74GHO6ArZP8Ww%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

前沿模型GPT-6 Astra，六档模型K2 Horizon，自动驾驶模型Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B，本地推理路由NVIDIA PAIR，音视频生成模型DreamX-Creator 1.0，多模态检索模型NeoMME。

> 9 月 4 日，今天值得关注的项目覆盖前沿模型、自动驾驶、本地推理、音视频生成与视觉文档检索：OpenAI 发布面向复杂端到端任务的 GPT-6 Astra，IFM 一次开放六档 K2 Horizon；本地侧则出现可调度多台设备推理请求的 NVIDIA PAIR。

**🧠 前沿模型**

**★ GPT-6 Astra｜OpenAI**

用 105 万 Token 上下文处理计算机操作、编程、研究和复杂多步工作，并在执行过程中持续调用工具。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=06dbdd02&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFYYDpXh6iaFeBbuAibY5B6QsEtHTAbPIwVBh06iaQaVibEYQb9SUNTDwY5DoO9UkSGbUB9w1lM5KyyZLN3s5zA5oQiczd9L8pLOZdfY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

OpenAI 于 9 月 3 日发布 GPT-6 Astra，模型 ID 为 **gpt-6-astra**。它支持文本和图片输入、文本输出，上下文窗口为 **1,050,000 Token**，最大输出为 **128,000 Token**，并提供 low、medium、high、xhigh、max 五档推理强度。

模型可通过 Responses API 和 Chat Completions 调用，支持 Streaming、Function Calling、Structured Outputs，以及 Web Search、File Search、Code Interpreter、Hosted Shell、Computer Use、Skills 和 MCP 等工具。标准价格为每百万输入 Token **10 美元**、缓存输入 1 美元、缓存写入 12.5 美元、输出 50 美元；当输入超过 272K Token 时，整个请求会采用更高费率。

**GPT-6 Astra 是闭源服务，没有开放模型权重。**当前首先向 Trusted Access Program 企业开放，ChatGPT Plus、Pro、Business、Enterprise 和普通 API 访问将在随后数日分批推出，不能写成已经对所有用户全面开放。

**上手门槛**

**在线使用**：🔴 高｜当前仅向少量 Trusted Access 企业开放｜其他付费计划分批推出

**开发接入**：🔴 高｜兼容 Responses API 与 Chat Completions｜当前仍受准入与分批开放限制

模型文档：<https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra>

使用指南：<https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model?model=gpt-6-astra>

安全说明：<https://openai.com/index/safety-overview-gpt-6-astra/>

**★ K2 Horizon｜IFM / MBZUAI**

一次开放从 0.9B 到 375B-A23B 的六档模型，并同步披露权重、训练代码、中间检查点和数据配方。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=04f1d6bd&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFYKkicD1RGEcRlxn7DjbZ3OEYqFeYTSdicB6FFtrddicnJGLzeuYbVJ0fUSKSAibib4Bbe0BPXlVm0cCr6wicP6XjK9KkATV7MurWnsA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

IFM 发布的 K2 Horizon 包含 **0.9B、3.7B、7B、32B、36B-A4B、375B-A23B** 六种尺寸，覆盖眼镜和手机等端侧设备、本地工作站以及企业级服务。36B-A4B 使用 Mixture-of-Value Attention（MoVA）和稀疏 MoE，每个 Token 约激活 4B 参数；375B-A23B 每个 Token 约激活 23B 参数。

这次开放不只包含最终权重，还覆盖训练代码、模型配置、数据混合、细粒度日志、评测结果和中间检查点；无法重新分发的数据则提供构建方法与配方。六档模型均支持量化，并获得 vLLM、SGLang 和 Ollama 的首日支持，可运行在 NVIDIA、AMD 和 Cerebras 平台。

模型与代码采用 **Apache-2.0**，数据集继续遵循 ODC-BY 等各自许可证，不能将全部训练数据统一写成 Apache-2.0。官方页面对部分训练基础设施和 Agent 强化学习代码仍使用“将发布”表述，具体材料是否齐全应以 Hugging Face 仓库实际文件为准。

**上手门槛**

**自行部署（0.9B—7B）**：🟢 低｜提供量化版本并支持 Ollama 等本地运行路径

**自行部署（32B / 36B-A4B）**：🟡 中｜需高内存工作站或高显存 GPU

**自行部署（375B-A23B）**：🔴 极高｜完整权重规模巨大｜需专业多卡服务器或集群

模型权重：<https://huggingface.co/IFM>

官方发布：<https://ifm.ai/blog/k2/>

**🔎 多模态检索**

**★ NeoMME｜H Company**

用同一个双向 Transformer 编码多语言文本和文档图片，为视觉 RAG 同时生成 Dense 与 Late-interaction 表示。

NeoMME 提供 **260M 和 800M** 两档多语言多模态编码器。它不使用独立视觉塔或因果语言解码器，而是把文本 Token 与 32×32 图像 Patch 输入同一个双向 Transformer；两档模型均支持 **16,384 Token 上下文**和动态图片分辨率，可直接处理包含排版、表格和图像信息的文档页面。

Retriever 版本在一次前向计算中同时输出单向量 Dense 表示和 128 维 Late-interaction 表示，可先通过 ANN 召回相关页面，再利用细粒度图文匹配进行重排。项目方报告，260M 版本在单张 L40S、2048×2048 输入和预处理 Tensor 条件下约为 **51 页/秒**；Late-interaction 索引可从平均约 1.5MB/页压缩至约 6KB/页，同时保留超过 95% 的基线 nDCG@10。

**NeoMME 是编码器，不是生成式视觉语言模型。**基础 Encoder 只输出上下文表征，不能直接完成文档问答；检索任务应使用 Retriever 版本，生成最终答案仍需连接外部 VLM。全部模型 Checkpoint 采用 Apache-2.0，官方同时提供可直接体验的视觉文档检索 Demo。

**上手门槛**

**在线使用**：🟢 低｜可通过 Hugging Face Space 直接体验视觉文档检索

**自行部署**：🟢 较低｜260M、800M 权重均已开放｜需使用较新版本的 Transformers 与 Sentence Transformers

在线体验：<https://huggingface.co/spaces/tonywu71/neomme-retriever-demo>

模型集合：<https://huggingface.co/collections/Hcompany/neomme>

官方介绍：<https://huggingface.co/blog/Hcompany/neomme>

**🚗 自动驾驶**

**★ Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B｜Qwen × 华中科技大学**

在同一个 4B 视觉语言底座中统一驾驶问答、3D 感知与未来 5 秒轨迹规划。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=fdce8e50&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFY5TXHzHKe6uyUxMxhxzUYImDXmeMnYMPXWuTGty3X0XhVc83agjTGnnLBuqSjibD9ibOGJib2CIpAZ0lOvXzMcQ3383NXQqLtDJQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

Qwen-Drive-1.0 由 Qwen Team 与华中科技大学联合发布，保留 Qwen3.5-4B 视觉语言模型的原始架构，并外挂 BEV Perception Head 与 Planning Expert。前者同时完成 3D 目标检测、语义占用预测和 BEV 地图分割，后者根据共享视觉语言表征生成自车未来轨迹；原有 LLM Decoder 则继续处理通用 VQA 与驾驶 VQA。

模型目录包含约 9.1GB 的根 VLM、各约 2.1GB 的 planner-sft 与 planner-rl，以及约 0.5GB 的 perception 模块。规划输出为未来 **5 秒、10Hz、50 个点**的轨迹；planner-sft 支持直接与推理规划，planner-rl 只在带推理的轨迹上做过奖励优化，建议配合 reasoning planning 模式使用。

官方建议使用 **24GB 以上显存**，仓库提供完整推理代码、四个规划 Demo 场景和六帧感知样例。项目采用 Apache-2.0；它目前属于自动驾驶研究基座和离线评测工具，不应直接等同于经过量产安全验证的车载系统。

**上手门槛**

**自行部署**：🟡 中｜建议 24GB+ 显存｜需安装 PyTorch、FlashAttention 与项目依赖｜感知模式包含 CUDA 算子

模型权重：<https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B>

ModelScope：<https://modelscope.cn/models/Qwen/Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B>

项目地址：<https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Drive-1.0>

**🛠️ 本地推理**

**★ NVIDIA PAIR｜NVIDIA**

自动发现局域网内可用设备，把多 Agent 的独立推理请求分配给运行 Ollama 或 LM Studio 的节点。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b3effbc2&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFa2iaPyG0V7r0PzCxoEKj5IPhsHVSnoeNP61OdJff0aYQEbJMmWmrbwgqR0oJKic0ia6kGu7duZI44KhgCoBZlmibfs0IAD8yvtUz0%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

NVIDIA Personal AI Router（PAIR）不是新的推理引擎，而是位于 Agent 与本地推理服务之间的路由层。它向应用暴露 Ollama 兼容和 OpenAI 兼容接口，再根据节点在线状态、推理引擎、目标模型是否存在、当前任务量与 GPU 利用率，把每个请求交给一个符合条件的设备执行。

PAIR 提供 Windows、Linux 和 macOS 安装包，可混合连接 RTX 20 系列及更新 GPU、RTX PRO、DGX Spark 和 Apple M4+ 设备。节点通过 mDNS 自动发现，也可按 IP 添加；用户确认配对后，节点间通信使用 mTLS 和自动生成的证书。

**PAIR 不会合并多台机器的显存，也不会切分模型或把一个请求跨节点执行。**它提升的是多个独立请求的并发能力。NVIDIA 在五个子 Agent 的特定演示中报告，三设备集群完成时间为 8 分 48 秒，单台 RTX Spark 笔记本约为 18 分钟；官方同时说明这不是通用 Benchmark，结果取决于任务并行度、模型、硬件和网络。

**上手门槛**

**自行部署**：🟡 中｜需至少两台同一局域网设备｜每个节点仍需独立安装引擎并具备加载目标模型的内存

安装下载：<https://github.com/NVIDIA/Personal-AI-Router/releases>

项目地址：<https://github.com/NVIDIA/Personal-AI-Router>

官方说明：<https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-pair-virtual-inference-router-expands-available-compute-on-your-local-network>

**🎬 音视频生成**

**★ DreamX-Creator 1.0｜高德 DreamX**

根据首帧图片和文本联合生成同步音视频，再用单步 Refiner 将画面提升至 2K。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=67a97a6a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFZbMSDWI5xuiaOLSjVcx9yoxkicWE5fnUFVwdAuNxE2yxTdrTDBsAKTD7ZYobWbqY9unUzXOwuj42XO1Rd2WDfcHopRkZGjQeQ0o%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

DreamX-Creator 1.0 于 9 月 3 日开放完整权重和推理代码。核心是一个 7B 原生音视频生成器：音频流和视频流先分别处理，再通过 Gated Cross-Modal Attention 双向交换信息，减少先生成视频、再单独配音带来的动作与声音错位。

生成阶段之后，5B SR-DiT 通过 Autoregressive 1-Step 2K Refinement 把视频提升到 2K。Refiner 也可单独处理外部视频，原音频保持不变。模型目录还包括 CreatorDACVAE、跨模态注意力权重、FlashLatentUpsampler，以及 Wan2.2-TI2V-5B 的 VAE 与文本编码器依赖。

官方提供单 GPU 推理入口、CPU Offload 和多 GPU Sequence Parallel 选项，但未给出统一最低显存数字。完整权重体积较大，生成器、Refiner 与依赖组件需要分别配置。项目采用 Apache-2.0，蒸馏版和更少采样步的加速模型仍在后续计划中。

**上手门槛**

**自行部署**：🟡 中｜需配置 7B 生成器、5B Refiner 与 Wan2.2 依赖｜官方提供单 GPU、CPU Offload 与多 GPU 路径

模型权重：<https://huggingface.co/GD-ML/DreamX-Creator>

ModelScope：<https://modelscope.cn/models/GD-ML/DreamX-Creator>

项目地址：<https://github.com/AMAP-ML/DreamX-Creator>

**🔎 多模态检索**

**★ NeoMME｜H Company**

用同一个双向 Transformer 编码多语言文本和文档图片，为视觉 RAG 同时生成 Dense 与 Late-interaction 表示。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=592d6c73&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFbtFjonbYxGZEdWHUsfCd13u0WnPLqCYrmucOTFhHoribic07sfCxibClr9gc5W2xgh8S0FraqkJbB5HAZ0qs7aF9aMHJwLKkDlRo%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

NeoMME 提供 **260M 和 800M** 两档多语言、多模态编码器。它不使用单独的视觉塔或因果语言模型，而是把文本 Token 与 32×32 图像 Patch 输入同一个双向 Transformer；两档模型均支持 16,384 Token 上下文和动态图片分辨率。

Retriever 版本在一次前向计算中同时输出单向量 Dense 表示和 128 维 Late-interaction 表示，可先用 ANN 召回页面，再利用细粒度图文匹配重排。官方报告，260M 版本在单张 L40S、2048×2048 输入和预处理 Tensor 条件下约为 **51 页/秒**；Late-interaction 索引可从平均约 1.5MB/页压缩到约 6KB/页，并保留超过 95% 的基线 nDCG@10。

**NeoMME 是编码器，不是生成式视觉语言模型。**基础模型只返回上下文表征，做文档检索应使用 Retriever 版本，生成最终答案仍需连接外部 VLM。全部模型 Checkpoint 采用 Apache-2.0；官方 Demo 可直接体验视觉文档检索。

**上手门槛**

**在线使用**：🟢 低｜Hugging Face Space 可直接体验视觉文档检索

**自行部署**：🟢 较低｜260M/800M 权重已开放｜需使用较新的 Transformers 与 Sentence Transformers

在线体验：<https://huggingface.co/spaces/tonywu71/neomme-retriever-demo>

模型集合：<https://huggingface.co/collections/Hcompany/neomme>

官方介绍：<https://huggingface.co/blog/Hcompany/neomme>

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=8c028879&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FUibyxhuYSuFYt0TTs9JRT4IWxcupdR1KlLayfiaslScrBpLvsGWn6aAH1alrFUCWE8R2LVqniaOIh5gXWOSB9Yicd0s0OXvDeDnyBy6FJRe25us%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

entries.title: Estimating a much stronger than usual El Niño
entries.content:
[![](https://flowingdata.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/relative-vs-regular-SSTA-tropical-Pacific-Aug9-Aug15-2026.png)](https://flowingdata.com/2026/09/04/estimating-a-much-stronger-than-usual-el-nino/)

For Climate.us, Emily Becker explains why it looks like [El Niño is going to break records this year](https://www.climate.us/news-features/blogs/enso/super-duper-or-el-nino-warming-world). Current estimates from NOAA adjusts for the ocean warming overall.

> Our old yardstick was telling us whether the El Niño region was warmer than average, but not if it was significantly warmer than other parts of the tropical oceans. Now we made a new yardstick: the Relative Niño-3.4 index, which is the original-flavor Niño-3.4 anomaly minus the average anomaly over the entire tropical oceans. Subtracting out the tropics-wide anomaly helps us understand El Niño’s true strength in a warming world. It’s very likely that this year’s action in the tropical Pacific is El Niño plus some climate change. To get just the ENSO part of the signal, we look at the Relative Niño-3.4 index.

It’s not obvious at a glance, but with the new model (top), you can see the stronger difference between blue on in the west and red on in the east. More variation leads to stronger El Niño.

**Tags:** [Climate.us](https://flowingdata.com/tag/climate-us/), [El Niño](https://flowingdata.com/tag/el-nino/), [estimation](https://flowingdata.com/tag/estimation/), [NOAA](https://flowingdata.com/tag/noaa/)

entries.title: Your wallet can sit out next week’s Apple event
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

On September 9, Apple is scheduled to hold its most anticipated hardware-centric event of the year. During the “[Surprise and shine](https://www.macworld.com/article/3221483/surprise-and-shine-apples-big-iphone-event-set-for-september-9.html)” keynote, Apple CEO John Ternus is expected to announce the all-new iPhone Ultra, alongside iPhone 18 Pro models, fresh Apple Watches, enhanced AirPods, and an overhauled smart home line.

While many of these devices will pack new hardware with a lot of hype behind it, it may be wise to skip buying your annual Apple upgrade this fall. Not only will iPhones be more expensive than ever, but many of the upgrades we’re expecting might not be worthy of an upgrade at all.

**Insufficiently Ultra**

Perhaps the event’s most exciting announcement will be the [iPhone Ultra](https://www.macworld.com/article/2629813/iphone-ultra-folding-design-display-specs-release.html). The first-generation product will mark Apple’s entry into the foldable market, rivaling Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 and the like. It’ll probably offer some neat benefits, like a more powerful iOS multitasking system and the ability to seamlessly switch between the small and large screen form factors. Essentially, it’s a hybrid device that blends an iPhone with an iPad mini. It all sounds great until you take a closer look at the full package.

![iPhone Ultra dummy unit](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/iphone_ultra_dummy_white_ice_universe.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Ice Universe

Despite its rumored Ultra branding, the foldable will sacrifice several iPhone features available on cheaper models. Most notably, it’ll downgrade biometric authentication from Face ID to Touch ID and exclude the telephoto camera that enables a longer zoom range. It may also come in just two lifeless colorways.

Taking its high cost into consideration, it’s hard to justify buying the iPhone Ultra. It’s usually advisable to steer clear of first-gen devices, especially when they cost $2,000-2,500 and aren’t as capable as the rest of the lineup. I’d recommend waiting for its successor, which will almost surely address some of the original iPhone Ultra’s shortcomings and potentially be more durable. Until then, using an iPhone and iPad separately provides a wider feature set and a longer combined battery life.

**Familiar Pro-file**

With the iPhone Ultra out of the way, you may be eyeing an [iPhone 18 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/2953687/iphone-18-pro-2026-release-date-design-specs-rumors.html) instead. After all, the Pro models are the most advanced and reliable of their kind, offering Apple’s latest innovations in the mobile department. Nevertheless, you’ll want to skip that, too.

![iPhone 17 Pro Max](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/iPhone-17-Pro-Max.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

The iPhone 18 Pro will likely introduce three core changes: a faster [A20 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/2910862/report-details-apples-next-gen-chips-lined-up-for-the-iphone-18.html) processor, a smaller Dynamic Island cutout, and new finishes. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro Max could solely get a variable aperture lens that helps elevate photography. While welcome, these upgrades will come at a cost, as the devices will reportedly see a $100-300 price hike. For most users, it’s wiser to buy a more fairly priced iPhone 17 Pro or wait for next year’s *[iPhone XX](https://www.macworld.com/article/3206297/20th-anniversary-iphone-2027-release-date-rumors-specs-features-price.html)*, which should be a dramatic overhaul that arguably warrants the upcharge.

**Watch from afar**

Beyond the new iPhones, the company is expected to announce the [Apple Watch Series 12](https://www.macworld.com/article/3177024/apple-watch-series-12-2026-design-features-specs-release-date.html) and Ultra 4 during its upcoming event. The smartwatches could feature the first performance boost in three years and an all-day heart rate monitor. There have also been some rumors about ceramic editions of the Series variants and an updated fitness tracking system.

But here’s the thing—all models from the Apple Watch Series 9 already support all of watchOS 27’s announced features, including Siri AI. They also continuously record your heart rate while you exercise and, otherwise, periodically do so throughout the day. That’s enough relevant data collection to give users a solid idea of their overall cardiovascular state. As for the refreshed fitness system, that will presumably be a watchOS 27 software perk that expands to all compatible models—not just the latest ones.

As such, if you use an Apple Watch Series 9 or newer, it’s best to skip upgrading this year and wait for the noticeably redesigned model rumored to launch as soon as next year.

**Sound decision**

Other mobile accessories I expect to see at the event are two AirPods 5 variants. Like the [AirPods 4](https://www.macworld.com/article/2463401/airpods-4-with-anc-review.html), the latest-generation wearable will provide optional active noise cancellation (ANC) for those willing to pay a bit more. Given that Apple typically offers its best audio technology in the AirPods Pro line, it’s unlikely that the AirPods 5 will introduce any meaningful features unavailable on [AirPods Pro 3](https://www.macworld.com/article/2921626/airpods-pro-3-review-small-improvements-make-a-sizable-difference.html). The refresh could be largely iterative, focusing on connectivity improvements and battery life. For something more exciting, I advise waiting for the [camera-equipped AirPods](https://www.macworld.com/article/3214440/wild-leak-straight-from-apple-shows-camera-equipped-airpods-in-action.html) rumored to debut in 2027, as they’ll enable major new capabilities.

![AirPods Pro 3](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AirPods-Pro-3.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

**Smart spending**

Apart from mobile devices, the “Surprise and shine” event will possibly feature Apple’s biggest smart home push to date. The Apple TV 4K and HomePod could leverage faster chips to unlock Siri AI. But let’s face it—your current smart speakers and set-top boxes can play music and movies just fine. While Siri AI is nice to have, it’s not an essential feature for media streaming devices.

![Using iPad Pro M4 as smart home hub](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Using-iPad-Pro-M4-as-smart-home-hub.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

More importantly, Apple could reveal its first-ever dedicated smart home hub, which some are calling the HomePad. The new device will use a new OS with a new interface, letting you easily view your smart home’s state and control HomeKit and Matter accessories. It’ll likely also support FaceTime calls, viewing News+ recipes, and other existing Apple services. Despite that, I still fail to see its unique selling point. The Apple TV 4K and HomePod already act as HomeKit hubs to power automations, remote control, and more.

iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and even watchOS all support interacting with smart accessories using the built-in Home app. Unless its exclusive use cases haven’t leaked yet, I see little reason why one would add a HomePad to their setup.

entries.title: Palms, neon, and Vice City vibes: How to preorder the limited-edition GTA 6 PS5 controllers
entries.content:
![The black and white Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition DualSense Wireless Controllers for PS5 on a purple and orange background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00mJ5p2cXflcAGlhItFama9/hero-image.webp)

Sony has officially unveiled two limited-edition DualSense controllers for [*Grand Theft Auto VI*](https://mashable.com/life/is-gta-6-cheating-tiktok), giving the [PS5](https://mashable.com/category/playstation) gamepads matching Vice City-inspired makeovers ahead of Rockstar's long-awaited sequel.

Both the black and white limited-edition [*GTA 6*](https://mashable.com/entertainment/gta-grand-theft-auto-6-xbox-series-x-s-playstation-differences) controllers are priced at $84.99 and are set for release on Nov. 19 — the same day as *GTA VI*.

Both controllers borrow heavily from Vice City's unmistakable aesthetic in different eye-catching ways. Both shells pack shimmering, color-shifting finishes that mix sunset hues with neon blues, plus custom palm tree details molded directly into the plastic and official *Grand Theft Auto VI* branding. If you’re a longtime *GTA* fan, the oversized ‘VI’ that’s taking over the touchpad will make this a must-buy.

![The white Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition DualSense Wireless Controller on a purple and orange background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00mJ5p2cXflcAGlhItFama9/images-5.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788511284.jpg)

Credit: Sony

The white model is taking cues from Vice City's beaches, pastel skies, and sunny day-glamor.

Meanwhile, the black edition is all about channeling the [gaming](https://mashable.com/category/gaming) city's nightlife. It's still got the same Florida-style palm trees, but in a more classically chic PlayStation black.

![The black Grand Theft Auto VI Limited-Edition DualSense Wireless Controller on a purple and orange background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00mJ5p2cXflcAGlhItFama9/images-6.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788511284.jpg)

Credit: Sony

The announcement on the [PlayStation Blog](https://blog.playstation.com/2026/09/03/first-look-at-the-grand-theft-auto-vi-limited-edition-dualsense-wireless-controllers/) does state that both will be available at "participating retailers," but for now, the only way to preorder the GTA VI DualSense controllers is through [PlayStation Direct](https://direct.playstation.com/) — starting on Sept. 10 at 7 a.m. PT/10 a.m. ET. Eligible orders placed directly through PlayStation will also get free launch-day delivery.

Stock will be available in limited quantities and will sell out fast. We’d advise bookmarking this article as a reminder and quickly jumping to the link above.

Beyond their new looks, they're still standard DualSense controllers, so they include haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. You'll get what you need as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story, but you won’t have any added features beyond the new, stylish aesthetics.

Keep in mind that although both *GTA 6* controllers officially launch on Nov. 19, exact availability will vary by country and region.

entries.title: The latest iPhone Ultra rumors and leaks: Everything we know about Apples first foldable
entries.content:
![a hypothetical render of the iPhone Ultrq on a stylized mashable background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01hptKeXP7rof9Beb3WAXlP/hero-image.jpg)

At this point, the foldable iPhone is the biggest open secret in Silicon Valley. Apple kept a tight lid on its first-ever [foldable phone](https://mashable.com/article/every-foldable-phone-2026) right up until dropping the iOS 27 developer beta, which includes some [direct and indirect references to the iPhone Ultra](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-ios-27-beta-hints-at-foldable-iphone) (also rumored to be called the iPhone Fold, iPhone Ultra Fold, or something else entirely).

Early adopters already love foldables — and [they have plenty of options](https://mashable.com/article/every-foldable-phone-2026) — but Apple's been notably absent from the genre. However, don't count Apple out. The company has a history of showing up late to the party and then absolutely cornering the market, as it did with AirPods and iPhones.

As we await official details, here's everything we know about the first foldable iPhone, including the latest rumors, specifications, release date, and pricing.

## When will the iPhone Ultra be released?

Apple has [officially confirmed an event for Sept. 9](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-announces-september-iphone-event-sept-9), where we're almost certain the iPhone 18 lineup will be unveiled. It's at this event where most expect the iPhone Ultra to make its real debut.

We think the iPhone Ultra will arrive on store shelves in fall 2026 alongside the [iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-18-latest-rumors-release-date-leaks-august-2026). Numerous [rumors](https://mashable.com/article/apple-iphone-fold-2026) pointed to this over the last year. Our best guess? We expect the iPhone Ultra to be released around Sept. 19; that's when the iPhone 17 launched last year.

Previous rumors suggested a delayed release schedule. Tech analyst named Tim Long [claimed](https://mashable.com/article/apple-iphone-fold-launch-date-report) that shipments of the iPhone Ultra wouldn't begin until December, but Bloomberg's Mark Gurman [threw cold water on this rumor](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-ultra-specs-mark-gurman-interview). And Gurman seems to have a crystal ball looking right into Apple headquarters these days.

A recent [report out of Australia](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-ultra-country-by-country-rollout) (via the Chinese supply chain) also claimed that the iPhone Ultra will be available right after launch in the U.S., though it might get rolled out to other markets a bit later.

## What will the iPhone Ultra look like?

We've seen a lot of iPhone Ultra leaks over the past year, but the most recent leak comes courtesy of YouTuber Unbox Therapy, which claims to have received dummy units from China. These leaks line up perfectly with the latest iPhone Ultra rumors and previous leaks.

The iPhone Ultra will have an aspect ratio and shape very similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but with more rounded corners. The rear of the device looks more like a Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, however. We believe the passport-shaped phone will have an external 5.5-inch OLED display and an internal 7.8-inch display. Leaks show two cameras on the rear of the device.

In addition to the Unboxed Therapy leak, the casemaker Benks has already posted product listings for iPhone Ultra phone cases.

![screenshot of benks website showing iphone ultra cases](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01hptKeXP7rof9Beb3WAXlP/images-6.fill.size_2000x1926.v1788463712.webp)

Credit: Benks

Finally, leaker Instant Digital reported earlier this year that the Ultra will have volume buttons on the top of the device rather than the side. "The volume buttons are not on the left side," reads a translation of the post. "Instead, they are placed directly on the top of the right-side frame (similar to the volume button layout on the top of the iPad mini). This may take some getting used to for users’ typical phone habits."

## How much will the iPhone Ultra cost, and will people buy it?

The iPhone Ultra is likely to be expensive. An early [estimate](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/fubon-expects-the-first-foldable-iphone-to-cost-2399-4375098) from research analyst Arthur Liao suggested the price tag for the Ultra — *gulp* — could come in around $2,399. Last year, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said the iPhone Ultra is [likely to retail](https://mingchikuo.craft.me/84AOn3Ll8Zah6f) between $2,000 and $2,500; recently, Kuo narrowed that down to $2,300 — $2,500. Finally, the International Data Corporation recently reported that the iPhone Ultra will have an average price of $2,550.

Despite the sizable cost (the flagship [Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8](https://mashable.com/tech/samsung-galaxy-z-fold-8) is priced at $1,899.99), sales expectations remain high. The IDC report estimated Apple would siphon 40 percent of the spending in the foldable market in 2026 and ship 17 million Ultras by the end of 2027.

"Apple’s entry into the foldable market has done more than reignite growth in a category that was losing momentum," wrote Nabila Popal, an IDC Senior Research Director, in [a recent report](https://www.idc.com/resource-center/blog/smartphone-shipments-set-for-record-16-7-drop-in-2026-as-the-memory-crisis-hits-full-force/)."With an average selling price exceeding $2,550, Apple is expected to generate more than $45.7 billion in value and account for over half of the category’s total value. Perhaps most notably, Apple is positioned to challenge Huawei and Samsung for leadership in markets where they have long dominated, an extraordinary outcome for a product expected to be less than two years into its lifecycle."

As of early September, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman is predicting a price tag of at least $2,000.

## The iPhone Ultra's potential specs

![hypothetical render of the iphone Ultra on a stylized background](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01hptKeXP7rof9Beb3WAXlP/images-2.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788463711.jpg)

What would you want to see in a foldable iPhone design? Let us know in the comments.
Credit: Zain bin Awais / Mashable

Based on all the available leaks, the iPhone Ultra specs could look something like this:

* **Displays:** 7.8-inch inner OLED display, 5.5-inch outer OLED display
* **Thickness:** 9.5mm unfolded, 4.5mm when folded
* **Security:** Touch ID
* **Processor:** A20 processor
* **Cameras:** Dual rear cameras (48MP), dual inner/outer front cameras
* **Price:** $2,399
* **Battery:** *At least* 5,088 mAh

The [foldable iPhone](https://mashable.com/article/foldable-iphone-cameras-touch-id) will be a book-style foldable with four cameras — two on the back, one on the inside, and one front selfie camera. Gurman also predicted it would use Touch ID like the iPad Air and Pro, even though iPhones typically use Face ID. All the recent leaks back up Gurman's reporting.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/SonnyDickson/status/2041395690598019402 "(Opens in a new tab)")

The smartphone market is already adapting to the expected size of the iPhone Ultra. [Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8](https://mashable.com/tech/samsung-galaxy-z-fold-8), which launched in July, is exactly that: A wider-than-usual foldable that looks like a proper tablet when unfolded. Huawei was the [first to market with a wide foldable](https://mashable.com/article/huawei-pura-x-max-video-iphone-fold), though the Pura X Max is only available overseas.

We've seen several [reports](https://9to5mac.com/2025/05/08/samsung-made-display-for-iphone-fold-said-to-be-more-advanced-than-galaxy-fold/) claiming that Apple has invested heavily in the iPhone Ultra's display and hinge. It should be very durable, thin, and with a barely visible crease, similar to the recent [Samsung Galaxy Z Fold](https://mashable.com/tech/samsung-galaxy-z-fold-8-ultra) devices. Samsung Display is reportedly producing the OLED displays for the iPhone Ultra, as Samsung's got the best flexible display tech in the game. There's a reason Samsung [released the Galaxy TriFold](https://mashable.com/article/samsung-galaxy-z-trifold-smartphone-sells-out-at-us-launch) while the world is still waiting on the first foldable iPhone.

Apple analyst [Ming-Chi Kuo](https://mingchikuo.craft.me/84AOn3Ll8Zah6f) reported earlier this year that the iPhone Ultra would have a 7.8-inch inner display, a 5.5-inch outer display, and measure in at just 9 to 9.5mm of thickness. Mark Gurman backed up these exact specs in September, just days before the big event. Rumors also indicate that Apple is using liquid metal for the phone's [hinge](https://x.com/mingchikuo/status/1902942517861159377), which should improve durability.

In a [recent update](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-08-23/apple-s-foldable-iphone-details-retail-store-changes-for-new-home-products-mt5vjf61), Gurman claimed that some early testers were pleased with how the Ultra performed, in particular with its look and feel, as well as the quality of its hinge. The camera, which doesn't have a telephoto unit, left something to be desired, the report said. Gurman's report confirms a lot of these rumored specs, and he reports that early testers also liked the more iPad-like UX and homescreen layout on the Ultra.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/Cartidise/status/2091740349643325497 "(Opens in a new tab)")

SEE ALSO:
[Foldable iPhone Ultra testers love the device except for these two things, report says](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-ultra-foldable-tester-reviews)

## What about the cameras and battery?

Leaker Instant Digital has made some interesting claims. Most notably, Instant Digital has said the iPhone Ultra will have the largest-ever iPhone battery. (For reference, the iPhone 17 Pro Max is estimated to have a roughly 5,088 mAh battery.)

Instant Digital's also stated, "The rear dual camera + right-side microphone + flash are arranged horizontally. The camera module appears to be fully black and does not match the body color. Currently, the only confirmed color is white, but it is expected that Apple will launch two color options."

Other sources have [confirmed](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-iphone-ultra-foldable-tester-reviews) the iPhone Ultra's dual-camera configuration, consisting of a regular and an ultra-wide camera.

## What does the iOS 27 beta tell us about the iPhone Ultra?

The iPhone Ultra isn't (yet) an official device. We do know a lot about it, but mostly via rumors, whispers, and reports coming out of Apple's supply chain.

But with the first [iOS 27 developer beta](https://mashable.com/tech/how-to-download-ios-27-ipado-macos-golden-gate-developer-betas-wwdc-2026), we finally learned some actual clues about the iPhone Ultra's existence. Software researcher [M1Astra](https://x.com/M1Astra) dug through the code (via [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-09/apple-s-ios-27-is-filled-with-hints-about-its-upcoming-foldable-iphone?embedded-checkout=true)) and found code that determines whether a device is folded or unfolded. Strings like “mechanicalAngleDegrees” and “angleDegrees" point to Apple fine-tuning the experience depending on how widely a foldable device is open. Researcher [Sam Henri Gold](https://x.com/samhenrigold/status/2064069948486320528/photo/1) found similar clues in the code.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/samhenrigold/status/2064069948486320528/photo/1 "(Opens in a new tab)")

That's not all. Certain widgets, such as Music, News, and Weather, can now be configured to take up the majority of the iPhone's display. That split-view doesn't make a ton of sense on a regular iPhone (you'd probably just want to have one app open instead), but on an iPhone Ultra, such a widget could occupy one side of the display while you do something else on the other.

![Apple Device Hub](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01hptKeXP7rof9Beb3WAXlP/images-5.fill.size_2000x1145.v1788463712.png)

Apple seems to be preparing developers to handle a larger variety of form factors. 
Credit: Apple

Then, at WWDC 2026, Apple's Senior VP of Software Engineering, Craig Federighi, pointed out a developer-specific feature called the [Device Hub](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/06/apple-aids-app-development-with-new-intelligence-frameworks-and-advanced-tools/), which allows developers to simulate their apps in different screen configurations.

Finally, [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/3159979/apple-left-some-major-folding-iphone-hints-in-the-ios-27-code.html) found references in the code suggesting a device that has both the Dynamic Island and a Touch ID; such a device does not exist today, but the iPhone Ultra is rumored to have both.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/MKBHD/status/2064146741809819728 "(Opens in a new tab)")

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/markgurman/status/2064118391280177360 "(Opens in a new tab)")

SEE ALSO:
[Apple's iPhone Fold is on track, but it might be pricier than we thought](https://mashable.com/article/apple-iphone-fold)

## What will the foldable iPhone be called?

Up until recently, most of the tech world has simply called the unannounced device the "iPhone Fold" or "iPhone Ultra." However, since it's not a confirmed product yet, it's very possible that the phone will have a different name at launch.

Most tech reporters have settled on the name iPhone Ultra, and that's what we're using until Apple tells us different.

## All the iPhone Ultra leaks we've seen so far

In December 2025, we saw lots of alleged iPhone Ultra renders circulating on social media, which all share a similar design.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/ShishirShelke1/status/2003714057552175278 "(Opens in a new tab)")

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/LeakerApple/status/2003395359910121895 "(Opens in a new tab)")

In February, a leaker known as [Instant Digital posted some alleged renders](https://m.weibo.cn/status/5261773869154461) of the iPhone to the Chinese social media site Weibo. Like most leaks, especially the ones pertaining to Apple, we can't confirm their authenticity. However, they align with earlier reports of the phone's overall look.

Apple leaker Sonny Dickson also shared another potential iPhone Ultra render in March 2026.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/SonnyDickson/status/2030841645827252668 "(Opens in a new tab)")

[Dickson shared](https://mashable.com/article/apple-iphone-fold-dummy-leak-size-comparison) more purported [dummy units of the iPhone Ultra](https://www.twitter.com/SonnyDickson/status/2030841645827252668) in April, giving those renders a bit more physicality than they had before.

April was fairly bounteous in terms of iPhone Ultra leaks. Aside from Dickson's dummy units, [YouTuber Vincent Zhong](https://www.youtube.com/@zhongwenze) got his hands on the [newly released (in Asia) Huawei Pura X Max Wide](https://mashable.com/article/huawei-pura-x-max-video-iphone-fold). This Chinese phone was one of the first real "wide foldables" to hit the market. It matches the overall design of iPhone Ultra leaks, and its screen dimensions are almost exactly the same as the alleged dimensions of the Ultra.

While the iPhone Ultra will almost certainly look different from Huawei's device, Zhong's hands-on video gives us a decent idea of what to expect from the iPhone Ultra as a physical object in your hands.

> [This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.](https://twitter.com/ShishirShelke1/status/2046193604826374169 "(Opens in a new tab)")

entries.title: Alienware’s latest OLED monitors are built for gorgeous visuals and stupid-fast gameplay
entries.content:
![Alienware monitors](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05LOGs7o0JK7xAp5oaO0YAM/hero-image.jpg)

**TL;DR:** [Alienware](http://mashable.com/tech/sep-1-alienware-monitor-deals) is launching two new OLED gaming monitors. The Alienware 32 4K OLED brings four-stack RGB stripe tandem OLED tech down from its 39-inch flagship into a 32-inch 4K panel. The Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED, co-developed with Team Liquid, is Alienware's fastest monitor ever — 560Hz, 0.03ms response time, DP2.1 with no DSC — arriving early Q1 2027 with pricing TBA.

---

[Alienware](http://mashable.com/tech/sep-1-alienware-monitor-deals) isn't picking a lane this fall — it's building two roads that go in opposite directions, and both are paved with OLED.

Unveiled at IFA in Berlin, the Alienware 32 4K OLED Gaming Monitor (AW3226Q) and the Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED Gaming Monitor (AW2527HX) split the difference between the two things [gamers](https://mashable.com/category/gaming) argue about at 2 a.m. on [Discord](https://mashable.com/article/discord-teen-experience-default): do you want the best-looking screen on your desk, or do you want to see the guy peeking the corner before he sees you? Alienware's answer is "why not both, just not on the same panel."

## Alienware 32 4K OLED

![Alienware 32 4K OLED](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05LOGs7o0JK7xAp5oaO0YAM/images-7.fit_lim.size_376x.png)

Credit: Alienware

![Alienware 32 4K OLED](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05LOGs7o0JK7xAp5oaO0YAM/images-8.fit_lim.size_376x.png)

Credit: Alienware

Alienware's 32-inch 4K OLED isn't a new idea for the brand — it's a trickle-down idea.

### RGB Stripe Tandem OLED, minus the fringing

Most OLED monitors use a four-subpixel layout, with an extra white subpixel added for brightness. Alienware ditched the white subpixel for a true RGB stripe arrangement instead, which means richer color volume since nothing's getting diluted, cleaner fringe-free text, and a polarizing layer that keeps blacks deep even with the lights on. Stack four emissive layers behind all that, and brightness climbs to 1,000 nits peak with an infinite (1.5 million:1) contrast ratio.

### Flat, traditional design

The design leans traditional on purpose — flat panel, 16:9, four-sided narrow bezels, wrapped in Alienware's Nova Black colorway as part of its "AW30" design language. If you're running a multi-monitor setup or just don't prefer curved screens, this design is built for you.

### Specs

You get ultra-vivid 99% DCI-P3 color with factory calibration precise enough to skip tweaking the settings, paired with a blazing-fast 4K 165Hz display and a 0.03ms response time for buttery-smooth action. Universal adaptive sync support keeps screen tearing at bay, no matter your graphics card, while dual HDMI 2.1 ports ensure current-gen consoles hit full resolution and frame rates, alongside DisplayPort and USB hub options.

## Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED

![Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05LOGs7o0JK7xAp5oaO0YAM/images-9.fit_lim.size_376x.png)

Credit: Alienware

![Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05LOGs7o0JK7xAp5oaO0YAM/images-10.fit_lim.size_376x.png)

Credit: Alienware

If the 32-inch is Alienware's answer to "make it beautiful," the 25-inch is Alienware's answer to "make it disappear." This is a monitor for people who consider 1080p a feature, not a limitation — because at 560Hz, resolution isn't the bottleneck, your reaction time is.

That 560Hz number is Alienware's fastest ever, paired with QD-OLED's 0.03ms gray-to-gray response time and a DisplayPort 2.1 (UHBR13.5) connection running at full bandwidth with zero DSC — nothing standing between your click and the pixel changing color.

Alienware calls it a generational leap over the TN panels that have dominated esports desks for years, backed by zero backlight bleed and 1,500-nit peak brightness.

### Built with Team Liquid, not just for them

Pro players from Team Liquid had direct input throughout development, and it shows in details that read like a wishlist from people who've actually LAN'd for a living.

The telescopic stand gets a 155mm adjustment range — with height and rotation markers so players can replicate their exact setup at any venue or LAN party. The base is small and rotatable, freeing up desk space for a keyboard angled diagonally underneath instead of squared off.

There's a dedicated esports button to instantly swap between 4:3 and 3:2 aspect ratios mid-session, plus a rear-flip headset hanger to keep peripherals off the desk entirely. Even the tilt range got the competitive treatment, with a generous 45-degree rear tilt for whatever posture gets you locked in.

### Designed to survive the long haul

Speed and image quality don't mean much if the panel degrades one season in, so burn-in protection gets the same longevity treatment as its sibling monitor. A graphite sheet disperses heat across the panel, an AI algorithm mitigates burn-in pixel-by-pixel, and pixel shift plus pixel refresh round out the defenses — all backed by the same 3-year warranty with OLED burn-in coverage.

### Specs

The Alienware 25 560Hz boasts an insanely fast 560Hz refresh rate and a 0.03ms response time, paired with DisplayPort 2.1 to drive full uncompressed bandwidth without needing Display Stream Compression. The matte anti-glare coating keeps reflections at bay under harsh tournament lights, while the OLED panel delivers standard-setting visual punch with infinite contrast.

Both monitors are VESA-certified for deep, true blacks and striking HDR contrast: the 25-inch 560Hz QD-OLED hits DisplayHDR True Black 600 for punchier peak highlights, while the 32-inch 4K model pairs DisplayHDR True Black 400 with Dolby Vision for dynamic, scene-by-scene precision.

## Pricing and availability

The Alienware 32 4K OLED arrives first, priced at $699.99, with global availability this fall. The Alienware 25 560Hz QD-OLED follows in early Q1 2027, with pricing to be announced closer to launch.

Two monitors, two totally different bets — one on eye candy, one on nanoseconds. Alienware's making the case that you shouldn't have to choose an OLED that's *either* gorgeous or fast. Just maybe not on the same desk.

entries.title: Enjoy the Windows 10 Update Experience at London's O2
entries.content: BORK!BORK!BORK! Windows 10 is lingering on after its friends have gone home, plaintively flickering out an update notification on a digital sign at London's O2 arena. The sign was advertising the venue and some of the activities available inside, including an indoor skydiving experience. We'd recommend indoor skydiving as an alternative to jumping out of a perfectly good aircraft for those minded to give it a go, although the sight of Windows 10 making its presence felt is less than ideal when considering undertaking an extreme sport. Indeed, a device bleating about a restart is not something one wants to think about just before you go inside and rely on the center's tech to safely blast you toward the ceiling using a fan mounted below the floor. Certainly, mid-air acrobatics would take on an entirely new frisson if there was the added danger of Microsoft's finest abruptly turning off the hardware to give itself a jolly good update. We've all been in that meeting when Windows decides a restart is needed mid-presentation. It's not great, and even less so when you're dressed in a jumpsuit, helmet, and about to venture into a column of air. Not that this hardware was part of the indoor skydiving activity, of course. The digital sign was showing an advertisement for the company beneath the notification. Rather, it's a very visible reminder of how much Windows 11 still has to do before it stamps its predecessor out of significance. According to Statcounter (not the most reliable source, but in the absence of official data from Microsoft, a useful indicator), Windows 11 currently enjoys a market share of just under 70 percent, while Windows 10 stubbornly hangs on at 30 percent. Windows 10 left support last year, although the security update lights can be kept burning for a few extra years via Microsoft's Extended Security Updates (ESU) program. In June 2026, Microsoft quietly extended the updates for consumers to 2027. Up to three years are on offer for commercial users. For a fee, of course. Microsoft's extension and the notification on O2's digital sign suggest Windows 10 isn't going anywhere anytime soon. Then again, considering how well things have gone for Windows 11 since release, perhaps it too would benefit from a blast of air from below to lift it convincingly above its predecessor. ®

entries.title: US law firm accuses UK AI software firm of unwanted contract renewal when it tried to leave
entries.content: A US law firm is alleging that UK-based telecoms and software company ConnexAI sold it software and AI systems that failed to perform as the vendor claimed, and then unlawfully renewed its contract. ConnexAI has rejected the allegations. The dispute has involves two court cases, both of which are ongoing. DK Law, a personal injury specialist based in California, alleged in a California court filing in April that ConnexAI promises “customers a telephone system and AI software solution with functionality that does not exist or perform as represented.” It also alleges in the California complaint [PDF] that ConnexAI continued to send it invoices after it had told the vendor it was not renewing the year-long contract. The Register understands that ConnexAI believes the allegations to be frivolous and without merit. The vendor is branded ConnexAI, and registered as Connex One Limited in the UK and Connex One Inc in the US. The customer’s claim followed a complaint that ConnexAI itself filed against the law firm the month before. In March 2026, in a New York court, ConnexAI filed a complaint [PDF] claiming its law firm customer had breached its contract by failing to pay invoices. Dan Richardson, ConnexAI general manager of North America, said in a statement: “There is a limit to what we can say while the matter is before the court. This claim is one part of a wider dispute which was initiated by Connex One Inc. The allegations now being made are rejected, and we would note that they were raised only after we issued proceedings which are active.” In its complaint in the US District Court, Central District of California, Southern Division, DK Law alleges that ConnexAI sold it a telephone system and software on the basis that it would provide phone and voice services integrated with SMS and WhatsApp. ConnexAI also said its Athena software included “sentiment analysis, entity recognition, call transcripts, interaction clustering, training cues, and the ability to identify trends.” Crucially, it also claimed the AI transcription worked in Spanish. “ConnexAI represented that the Athena AI software included AI Agent, AI Guru, AI Analytics, AI Voice, Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), all of which were represented to elevate customer interactions and enhance customer engagement and experience,” the filing said. Using AI agents would offer around-the-clock availability, faster response times and personalized interactions, with a “human-like voice and text-based communication,” the complaint argued. After less than a year using the software, DK Law alleged its experience of the software differed from the claims made by the vendor. According to the California filing, the telephone system frequently “went down”, with calls often dropped or unanswered. Calls were also consistently misrouted, the customer alleges. The problems were reported to the vendor’s support team. After the issue was escalated, the filing continues, ConnexAI sent US technical services engineers and the UK-based CTO to troubleshoot. “Sometimes the problem was resolved for the moment, only to recur shortly thereafter, with no permanent fix,” the complaint claimed. In addition, WhatsApp was unreliable and effectively unusable, DK Law alleges. While ConnexAI had claimed its ASR “would never miss a word,” DK Law claimed “this too was false.” Per the filing, on checking recordings of calls, the customer claims to have discovered that only a few seconds of a conversation were actually recorded despite evidence of a longer call. “Connex also represented in pre-contract discussions that its software was able to create real-time call transcripts of customer interactions conducted in English and Spanish. However, in reality, the Connex software only sometimes produced a transcript. When compared to the recorded conversations, DK Law found the transcripts of calls conducted in English to be inaccurate, and the Spanish language transcription did not work at all,” the California law firm alleged. Given the performance, the filing claims, Brendan Haverlock, DK Law CTO, told the vendor that the contract would not be renewed after it expired in October 2025. But that was not the end of the matter. The complaint alleges ConnexAI continued to invoice DK Law after the end of the contract term, demanding payment and "harassing its employees" for payment, the customer alleged. In March 2026, Connex Inc, the US company, launched a legal claim in the New York case against DK Law in which it alleged DK Law had failed to make the required payments and breached its contract. The filing, which was originally made in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, and then moved to a New York District Court, said that in October 2024, the two companies entered into an agreement, which “renewed for a subsequent term commencing on October 8, 2025.” However, in the separate but related California filing in April, DK Law alleged that ConnexAI had already breached the contract “by failing… to implement and deliver telecommunications and software services in a manner consistent with industry standards.” It also said in the filing that ConnexAI's claim that the contract had automatically renewed was not in accordance with New York State law, which “required Connex to give written notice of the automatic renewal in advance.” The law covers telecommunications and software. ConnexAI “never provided the requisite notice of automatic renewal,” DK Law alleged. In the California Court, DK Law seeks restitution and damages. In a statement to The Register, ConnexAI’s Richardson questioned why Connex One Ltd was included on the California claim, given Connex Inc sued DK Law in New York. In the California filing, DK Law alleged the UK company “directly participated in the sales process, provided or controlled implementation and support personnel, and directed or ratified the post-notice renewal and retention conduct.” It said the US company is wholly owned and operated by the UK’s Connex One Limited and acted as a contracting arm or agent. The case is now waiting to move through the courts. Last week, (August 27) the California court denied DK Law’s claim, but only insofar as it “stayed” the case, pending the New York claim. In effect, that case is put on hold until the New York case is settled. DK Law is attempting to have the New York case dismissed and has requested the court hear oral arguments. On September 1, in an order and opinion filed by federal magistrate judge Katharine H Parker, the motion to stay the case was denied [PDF].® Reg note: We are not accepting comments on this article and have closed the forum.

上周参加了在世界机器人大会

正如 Arm 物理 AI 全球负责人 Federico Pecora 在大会上所言：物理 AI 正从“单点能力验证期”跨入“系统攻坚期”。  
  
今天的机器人单项技能并不弱，但真正进入开放环境，考验的是一整套系统能力。视觉感知、语言理解、路径规划、毫秒级运控与安全底线，必须在同一套硬件架构中实时动态协同...  
  
Arm 并不造机器人，但在为物理 AI 构筑坚实的计算底座。从端侧传感器、实时控制器到高算力芯片，Arm 正让机器人的“大脑”与“小脑”无缝协同，加速具身智能真正走进现实生活。

entries.content:
著名播客潜空间对GPT6-Astra 的长篇评论，集合了多方评测，简单总结：  
  
1. GPT6-Astra 在 Coding Agent能力上与Claude Opus 5、Fable 5差不多，但落后于 Fable 5.1。  
  
综合智能指数，部分维度甚至落后于GPT5.6。  
优势是Token效率高，特定任务很优秀，比如Computer Use等。  
  
2. 评测中的Harness差异：ARC Prize的评测发现，ARC-AGI-3只有在OpenAI的特殊适配Harness上达到99%，标准跑分是63%。  
  
以后评测都要说明是否用了专有Harness，否则容易误导。  
  
3. 思维链监控失效：在没有Cot情况下，自主运行从3.6分钟提升到30.9分钟。  
  
也就是说，模型不显示推理过程，能完成更复杂的任务，这也带来了潜在安全风险。  
  
4. Astra 是OpenAI历史上最受关注的模型发布之一。  
  
9小时3600万浏览、16.4万点赞（X上？），最近第一次超过Anthropic公司模型发布的声量。  
  
5. 特色优势  
GPT-6 Astra 主打Computer Use、自主软件编程和长流程复杂任务处理。  
  
在 3D 建模、重建（如 Blender 与 Unreal）、数学与科学推理上取得突破，解答了 Lean 验证的未解 Erdős 问题。  
  
6. 模型定价  
  
标准版为百万 Tokens 输入 $10 、 百万Tokens输出 $50  
  
2.5倍速 Fast 版为 $20 / $100，价格翻倍。  
  
单 Token 价格比 GPT-5.6 Sol 增长 2.5 倍。  
  
但因为 Token 效率显著提升（编程任务仅用前代约三分之一 Token），所以单任务成本只有一半。

entries.title: 我国启动国际地月立方星座大科学计划，填补全球地月空间系统性观测空白
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，据新华社报道，今天（4 日）举行的 2026 年深空探测（天都）国际会议宣布，我国正式启动**国际地月立方星座大科学计划**，拟联合多个国家在**地月空间部署卫星群**，立体组网开展空间环境监测、伽马射线暴探测、月球资源勘探等工作，初步计划 2030 年左右完成全部卫星发射部署，**填补全球地月空间系统性观测空白**。

地月空间从地球低轨道延伸至距地球约 200 万公里，是人类拓展活动空间的新空域，也是未来载人登月与月球基地建设的核心活动区域。长期以来，人类对其认知主要依赖单点探测，存在时空覆盖不足、关键区域数据匮乏等问题，亟需开展系统性连续观测。

据介绍，此次大科学计划将在地月共振大椭圆轨道、环月轨道等位置部署卫星群。30 颗重量不超过 30 公斤的 12U 立方星，将分 6 批部署至 1∶3 地月共振大椭圆轨道，组成空间环境监测、伽马射线暴探测星群。依托多星多点同步观测，可完整捕捉空间天气事件演化过程，将伽马射线暴定位精度提升至亚角秒级。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/46969c52-3667-49d0-8c7f-0b086608edf8.jpg)

图源：Pexels

IT之家从报道中获悉，该计划由深空探测实验室与国际深空探测学会共同发起，亚太空间合作组织支持，确立“**联合设计、免费搭载、经费各担、科学数据共享**”的国际合作原则。中方统一研制高能粒子成像、空间磁强计、伽马射线暴探测三套标准载荷，免费向合作方提供。项目还将开展技术培训、制定统一接口标准，助力发展中国家深度参与深空探测。

目前，**泰国、塞尔维亚、埃及、塞内加尔、印度尼西亚**等多国科研机构已加入该计划，第一阶段工程研制已启动，卫星、载荷、测控等大系统总体方案论证即将完成。项目建成后，将推动地月空间探测**从单点断续模式向网络化连续观测转变**，为载人登月生命安全及地月空间环境前沿科学研究提供核心数据支撑。

国际深空探测学会副理事长胡朝斌表示：“我们期待和全球伙伴一道，共同拓展人类对深空宇宙的认知边界。”
entries.summary: 我国正式启动国际地月立方星座大科学计划，建立网络化深空系统观测。

entries.title: NHTSA 对特斯拉 Cybercab 安全标准认证启动审查，预计涉及 1000 辆车
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 4 日消息，据路透社报道，美国国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）对**约 1000 辆特斯拉 Cybercab** 展开审查，重点调查特斯拉用于**证明该车型符合联邦车辆安全标准**的认证流程和技术数据。

当地时间 3 日，在特斯拉开始于得克萨斯州奥斯汀商业运营少量双座 Cybercab 后，审查随即启动。特斯拉表示，未来计划逐步增加运营车辆数量，并扩大服务覆盖范围。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/526a4686-5d22-494f-8c8c-cea83b218bec.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

NHTSA 指出，Cybercab 没有永久固定的传统人工控制设备，包括**方向盘、刹车踏板、加速踏板和后视镜**。

据IT之家了解，审查将涉及特斯拉认证依据等问题，其中包括特斯拉如何判断部分联邦机动车安全标准不适用于 Cybercab。

得克萨斯州政府数据显示，截至当地时间周五上午，特斯拉在该州登记的自动驾驶车辆数量为 420 辆，其中 4**5 辆为 Cybercab**。

entries.title: 奥特曼押注AI效率，扎克伯格却要开发者保住退路：别把产品锁死在一个模型上
entries.content:
原创 姜篇 2026-09-04 18:00 日本

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1b66fc26&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgJn2JicowZzgTrzTXOrkQicWuBvHPCibrCEyW3IQe0ugXjesz4BEx64uzydzM066JkicGMyibsqTYwaZ2ttK8qRukUDLYKhB8Jqlygw%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

Sam Altman押注AI效率，扎克伯格却要开发者保住退路：别把产品锁死在一个模型上

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b6a4647d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FMOwlO0INfQoIDJ0nx1IhNibpIpYLrpUE0kIP9qbF1iaY7EoZpaic6IojvbXibd5ZGiatxmjtibQRcVbGAPM9Ijvp66yQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2a93b330&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIHbsh8dE6dQ3zfFfVLIiaDfxhDibRykvL8qEEyrZCTdAtR1zfo7EdkdFSvHERET1kOklEGm28FGqICxMtjRq57TJmDicV74giaoicM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

编辑 | 姜篇

> “Three months is now probably doable in 17 minutes with Codex.”
>
> Sam Altman：过去需要一家创业公司忙三个月的工作，现在用Codex，可能17分钟就能完成。

三个月，压缩到17分钟。

山姆·奥特曼在G20创新部长会议上用这个数字描述AI带来的开发速度。做原型、补接口、生成测试、修改代码，很多过去按周排期的任务，正在变成一次Agent会话。

就在同一场会议，扎克伯格关注的却是另一件事：

> “It puts the power in individual developers’ hands.”
>
> 扎克伯格：开源把控制权交到了每个开发者手里。

当AI开始参与整个开发流程，模型就不再只是一个提高效率的工具。它可能读取公司的代码、调用内部系统，甚至决定一项任务该怎样完成。

问题也随之出现：如果这些能力全部建立在同一家模型公司的接口上，模型涨价、下线或改变安全策略时，开发团队还有没有办法切换？

山姆·奥特曼讲的是AI能把软件做得多快。扎克伯格关心的是，软件做出来以后，控制权还在不在开发者手里。

这两场发言放在一起，刚好说中了AI开发正在出现的新矛盾：**代码越来越便宜，离开模型平台却可能越来越贵。**

以下为两人在G20创新部长会议上的发言，我们进行了翻译与整理。

## **三个月压成17分钟，先被压缩的是试错成本**

Sam Altman谈到创业时，用了一个非常具体的例子。

过去，一家创业公司可能要用三个月做出第一版产品。现在，借助Codex，这段工作有机会被压缩到17分钟。

他说的重点不在“17”这个数字有多精确，而在于测试一个想法的成本正在迅速下降。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=dc0f4d5c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgLMfXSbozGDTNkVXu2PpicetTsnyCkGicEXMRTmAdO6UVIiaW4icprAhnNcEqnYwdiaicv2Q4YPdkfXgnYnDNUurviaKhm86mEob1TXEQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Sam Altman谈Codex如何压缩创业团队的开发时间*

这个判断放到开发现场并不陌生。搭一个后台、补一批接口、生成测试、写部署脚本，以前要排进迭代，现在可以在一次会话里跑出初版。

但初版来得越快，后面的选择越难躲开：代码接哪套模型，数据发到哪里，模型更新后要不要重新评测，供应商调整价格时能不能切走。

AI省下了第一笔开发成本，也提前带来了第二笔架构成本。

## **扎克伯格想把Agent交到更多人手里**

扎克伯格在9月1日的发言里，把开源和Agent放在了一起。

他的设想是，未来的个人Agent不应只掌握在少数公司手中。普通用户、创业团队和独立开发者都应该能拿到模型，按照自己的需要改造和部署。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=ac00be80&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJDSHDQ4fylS3fQ8je2icuOWFDYPGOTzXZeBHpWm3voBDpsKBAM4j6ooDhhJALqDkpw2A1GD9EUscG8iapVJh4wibtePTFBS1Q3ws%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Mark Zuckerberg谈个人Agent不应只掌握在少数公司手中*

这和“免费用一个聊天机器人”不是一回事。

如果Agent要长期读取邮件、代码仓库、项目文档和业务数据，团队迟早要回答几个现实问题：它运行在哪里，记住了什么，谁能查看记录，出了错以后谁有权把它停下来。

模型只提供调用入口时，这些规则很大一部分由平台决定。模型可以自己部署和修改时，团队才有机会把选择权拿回来。

## **开源在扎克伯格眼里，首先是一种开发者控制权**

> “It puts the power in individual developers’ hands.”
>
> 扎克伯格：开源把控制权交到了每个开发者手里。

他说，开发者不该长期依赖少数前沿模型实验室。

> “Not just dependent on a small number of these frontier labs.”
>
> 扎克伯格：不能只依赖少数几家前沿模型实验室。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=4802d126&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJ4MPQKbYhk6YEm8MLS2ZSXGiaJ577RzNTRcNns7LMibYsMOicLlABVgmjFsBWb3jOAt5SrzkYfZfwGqr8oMdRj1OPCPsDHVdDveM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Mark Zuckerberg谈开源模型与开发者控制权*

这句话很容易在真实项目里找到对应场景。

一个团队把客服、代码审查或数据分析全部接到同一家模型供应商。半年后，模型名称变了，旧版本停止服务，价格重新计算，安全策略也更严格。原来的提示词跑不稳，工具调用开始被拒绝，团队只能跟着上游重新改系统。

这样的风险和模型今天排第几关系不大。只要应用把上下文格式、工具协议、评测标准和业务逻辑都写死在一家平台上，换模型就会变成一次迁移工程。

开发者真正需要保留的，是切换模型的能力。

## **更多人能检查模型，安全问题才有机会被看见**

扎克伯格还为开源安全给出了一套解释。

> “More secure because there’s more scrutiny.”
>
> 扎克伯格：更多人参与检查，系统才可能变得更安全。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=3edebd3c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJNys3lnofyBT7iaM89rgj0qtiblic6Jicuo2Ls5Tu64icbJlf1UyyhZos5asNgUjVFaV8GMibe6DWWdBwRItrkGIicKnfJKLlZCd5wv8%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Mark Zuckerberg解释公开审查为什么可能提高模型安全性*

闭源模型出了问题，外部开发者往往只能提交工单，等待平台修复。开放模型允许研究人员和工程团队检查实现、复现缺陷，再把修复方法公开出来。

不过，开源不会替项目自动完成安全工作。

模型权重开放以后，依赖包、推理服务、提示注入、工具权限和数据泄露仍然要逐项处理。能看到问题，只是获得了修复问题的条件。

Meta自己的态度也留有边界。

扎克伯格明确表示，Meta同时开发开放模型和封闭模型，是否开源会逐个模型评估。开源是它的重要路线，并不是每一个模型都会无条件放出。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e770063d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgImInI9OJF55wTYp1g00SAVXQJ0CO9H3f3Jpmia9YE4JNz6XG2jVsrqfdvQOHibs7AiccV1RA1jMcYlz9lgYYvOdicibEVnkZgdiaDNM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Mark Zuckerberg表示Meta会逐个评估模型是否适合开源*

这段补充很重要。把开源写成一句口号很容易，真正决定开发者是否拥有控制权的，还包括许可证、权重可得性、训练资料、部署门槛和后续版本能否持续获得。

## **AI会像电力一样普及，团队仍要决定哪些能力自己掌握**

奥特曼在第二天用了另一个比喻。

> “Not having AI would be like not having electricity.”
>
> Sam Altman：不用AI，最终会像一百年前拒绝接入电力一样难以想象。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7226e82b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJ4pROIQOBYJVR7VibJR17WXEiaB5NSxk1YKAT59zLx8xsBCW9MNhzFYfECVzV02CL9C1ibpvBCcQ4fj6ZpEVz5EichISicLTJ2x4Po%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Sam Altman把AI的普及类比为接入电力*

AI如果真的变成基础设施，企业不会因此全部自建模型。数据库、云服务器和支付系统早就证明，关键能力可以购买，但架构不能假装供应商永远不变。

奥特曼把这个选择概括成了三个词：

> “Build versus rent.”
>
> Sam Altman：哪些能力自己建，哪些能力向平台租。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=30878778&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgLXHEVia9S2hUgR8bGhr9sOfAgaeTILjjYL88n7ty5iaYKc5c6kMgsMHb1GTAUwYsjdHpwZxniao2eQlg39cKJibxbAX0yMbSkKRo4%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Sam Altman谈企业如何选择自建或租用AI能力*

对普通开发团队，自己训练基础模型并不现实。能掌握在手里的，是模型之上的那一层：统一的调用接口、自己的上下文和数据、可重复运行的评测集、与模型分离的工具权限，以及随时可以启用的备用模型。

做到这些，Claude、GPT、Gemini或开源模型才是可替换的执行组件。否则，产品看起来接入了很多AI能力，底层仍然只有一个开关。

## **安全和平台依赖，最后都会落到工程细节**

奥特曼在现场提到，他当前最担心的风险之一是网络安全。模型开始操作终端、仓库和云服务后，一次错误不再只生成一段坏答案，它可能真的修改文件、泄露密钥或者触发部署。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=07ac8f3b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgI5dpCREAy4cribliar3LwKZDj0FAw9OOQHSN1pEeiaVm5q2zH0Eq4o5VHudFclDKUgf081UKVAmzVnibhTUia3weUc9RvKPNJlEkus%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Sam Altman谈AI进入工具和系统后的网络安全风险*

这类系统至少要把四件事留在模型之外。

工具权限需要分级。读取仓库、修改代码、访问生产数据库和发布版本不能共用一把钥匙。

过程需要留痕。Agent看过哪些文件、调用过什么工具、为什么作出修改，应该能被复查。

高风险动作需要人工确认。删除数据、付款、上线和调整权限，不能因为模型判断“任务已完成”就直接执行。

系统还要准备退路。模型不可用、输出质量下降或接口发生变化时，应用应该能降级、切换和回滚。

开源模型提供了另一种部署选择，闭源平台提供了更省事的服务。真正影响生产安全的，仍是团队有没有把权限、记录和失败处理写进系统。

## **评论区讨论起了“到底能不能信Meta”**

扎克伯格谈完开源，评论区很快分成了几种声音。

有人直接支持Meta继续开放模型，认为开发者需要更多可选方案。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=946b6f0a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIBbFl2UqWwQbBhX9g9wlBkQr5C5wXmX4lE7FicHcZ8TQVUZrkVkDFcyVKFuVhKSPvIL9CvribuAvgI3GJddVnyKMX6HFAY1SslA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

也有人担心，企业发布的开源技术仍可能存在无法发现的后门，公司的历史信用会影响开发者是否愿意采用。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e4bbebcd&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIub8xPwZTnZoPVhZISicqNxl9ffrHbnrLaRZbkLE2o5HXaV3MicIdHqEiaKQyKPTicF7r3ew1NYMTiaVgewdw0VRO8BXcbIJMRfEzc%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

还有人把问题指向了财富和权力集中：即使模型开放，真正有能力训练、部署和分发AI的公司仍然有限。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9ece5de1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgLqXNxI6NuianficeGIyTweSJnAsL0gyLJscPRPP72rw3WAX65uycfcwpvXMpLmrJQlXoEzOH50ibUdJj8nUZFBvibVScn1EIEbzPY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

这些留言不能代表整个开发者社区，却把开源AI绕不开的矛盾摆了出来。大家希望减少对少数平台的依赖，同时也不会因为代码或权重可以下载，就自动相信发布它的公司。

## **写在最后**

17分钟做出第一版产品，正在从夸张故事变成可以亲手验证的工作方式。

一年后，模型涨价了、旧版本下线了、安全策略变了，产品还能继续运行，才是开发团队真正留下来的能力。

调用最强模型并不难。保住模型选择权，需要从项目第一天就把上下文、评测、权限和回滚握在自己手里。

开源能多给开发者一个选择。这个选择能不能变成控制权，最终还要看系统怎样设计。

entries.title: Apple's suppliers only made a few hundred iPhone Ultra units per day in August
entries.content:
Mass production of the [iPhone Ultra](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-fold "iPhone Fold") has been underway for at least some weeks, but quality control inspections are reportedly rejecting all but a few.  
  

![Foldable smartphone partially open on a wooden desk near a small potted succulent and a cute glowing cat-shaped lamp, with warm natural light from a nearby window](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68836-145024-000-lede-iPhone-Ultra-xl.jpg)  
The expected iPhone Ultra is still believed to be announced at the September 9 event, but supplies may be extremely constrained.

  
Reports have varied for months over whether the iPhone Ultra is delayed because of [manufacturing problems](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/06/16/strident-leaker-insists-iphone-fold-is-not-delayed-at-all), or whether those have [been resolved](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/08/03/iphone-fold-is-on-schedule-for-september-after-manufacturing-problems-are-solved). Now according to *Nikkei Asia*, however, production has been very slow.  
  
Reportedly, Apple introduced a further inspection and verification process for the device during August. An unspecified source said that the additional process is concerned with production quality rather than there being manufacturing problems.
